# Hangar screen needs more detail about the various options

> **Producer request (verbatim):** "On the hanger screen add an information
> panel in the center of the screen, between the unlocks and the equip sections.
> This panel should show more information about the currently selected option.
> Also group the different sections into logical units and improve the layout.
> Use the design language developed for the hex map screen."

## Problem statement

The hangar screen presents every hangar-war option as a single terse row
(`Bulwark Hull — 220 min · 3 cores — BUY`, `HULL Scrap Hull — EQUIPPED`,
`MODIFIER Ablative Plating — ON`), so a player can see a price but not what an
option **does**. The authored one-line `description` on every catalogue entry is
never rendered, a hull's defence/run stats and granted skill are invisible, a
modifier's effect is not spelled out, a power-up's level and six-slot cap are
only implied, and the ▶ DEPLOY row does not say what the launch will actually
carry. On top of that, seven headings (`TARGET INTEL`, `UNLOCKS`, `HULLS`,
`LOADOUT`, `MODIFIERS`, `SAVED BUILDS`, plus the four fixed bottom rows) sit in
two bare, unframed columns, so the purchase tree, the deployment selector and
the meta controls read as one undifferentiated list.

## Users

- **The first-time hangar player** — "I have 260 minerals and three hulls on
  screen; what does each one change about my run, and what is it worth?"
- **The between-sortie player** — "Before I press DEPLOY, show me the hull,
  weapons, modifiers and target I am launching with, in one place."
- **The player who cannot rely on colour** — "Detail must be readable without
  hue; the `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` marks must survive (repo CVD policy)."
- **The producer / maintainer** — "One model and one renderer for the game and
  `GymHangar`, one design language shared with the hex map, and no second
  pricing/equip rule invented inside the screen."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Moving focus (keyboard `tab`/arrows, and pointer hover) onto any hangar row
  updates a **centre detail panel** that names the option and shows its detail:
  the catalogue `description`, the option's kind-specific facts (a hull's base
  defence, upgrade levels, run stats and granted skill; a weapon's matchup
  verdict and permanent level/cap; a modifier's effect in words; a power-up's
  installed/off/blocked state, level and cap), and its price / owned / gated /
  shortfall state — every fact sourced from the shipped catalogue and the
  existing pure economy verdicts, with **no new gameplay number invented** in
  the screen.
- With **no row focused** (screen open, focus dismissed) the centre panel shows
  the **deployment summary** the ▶ DEPLOY row will launch — hull, starting
  weapons, modifiers, power-ups and target hex — built by the existing pure
  deployment builder, so the panel can never describe a launch the screen does
  not perform.
- The screen is grouped into **bounded, headed, hairline-framed panels**
  (rounded frame, faint fill, monospace heading) taken from the hex map's
  design language, with the panels registered in a single-source rect table
  published on the view (one `{ key, heading, rect }` per section, in reading
  order) — purchase tree and `TARGET INTEL` left, the new detail panel centre,
  the deployment selector and `SAVED BUILDS` right, the fixed buildout / restart /
  map / deploy rows in one framed actions block.
- Layout invariants are **tested, not eyeballed**: every section rect lies
  inside the 960×540 frame, no two rects overlap, every row's Y falls inside its
  own section's rect, no row collides with the fixed bottom-row block, and each
  row's label fits its column at its font size (the shared
  `wrappedLineCount`/`sectionBudgetHeight` budget, not a live canvas).
- `GymHangar` renders the **identical** sections, headings and detail panel
  read-only from the same model, with no handler and no new scene-local rule
  (gym↔game parity), and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the new panels.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, the module docblock of `hangarScreen.ts`, GDD §8.2's hangar-screen
  description, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and the `GymHangar` row.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now see what each hangar option actually does — its description,
stats, effect and price — in one centre panel before committing salvage or
pressing deploy, instead of guessing from a one-line row.

## Constraints

- **Presentation only.** No purchase, equip, upgrade, banking, deployment,
  reset or attract rule may move into the screen: every verdict stays with
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` and `./hangarDeployment` (the screen
  only presents and applies them through the shared pure updaters). No
  catalogue balance change.
- **Fixed 960×540 frame, no scrolling.** `src/core/constants.ts`
  (`GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`) — the whole screen must still fit the worst case
  (full catalogue, full loadout, saved builds present) with nothing clipped and
  no row overlapping another. A three-column split (tree | detail | selector)
  is the producer's stated arrangement, so a row label may **shorten** to a
  state chip (`BUY`, `LV 2/3`, `NEED 40 min`) with the long form moving into the
  detail panel; the row-fit test above pins that trade.
- **One screen code path** (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity): `buildHangarScreenModel`
  and `renderHangarScreen` remain the single pair the game's `HangarScene` and
  `GymHangar` both consume; the detail content must be part of the **model**
  (pure, table-testable), not computed inside the renderer.
- **Design language is single-sourced**, not copied: reuse the hex map's
  exported geometry/budget helpers (`wrappedLineCount`, `sectionBudgetHeight`,
  `sectionBodyWidth`/`sectionBodyHeight`) and share the frame drawing (extract
  `drawSectionPanel` + the fill/stroke/padding constants into a neutral shared
  module consumed by both `hexMap.ts` and `hangarScreen.ts`) so the two screens
  cannot drift in look.
- **CVD-safe**: no information conveyed by colour alone — state words/markers
  (`OWNED`, `BUY`, `▲ EFFECTIVE`, `▼ RESISTED`, `BLOCKED`) accompany every tint.
- Fixed-row behaviour is preserved: the two-step `⟲ RESTART WAR` confirm, the
  `⚡ APPLY SUGGESTED BUILDOUT` row, the auto-fit-on-open rule and the attract
  bot's single next action must all behave exactly as today.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (≈2.7k lines) builds the pure
  `HangarScreenModel` (`unlockRows`, `hullOptions`, `weaponOptions`,
  `powerUpOptions`, `modifierOptions`, `savedBuildRows`, `bossIntel`,
  `buildoutRow`, `mapRow`, `restartRow`, `deployRow`, `focusOrder`) and renders
  it with two hard-coded columns (`LEFT_X = 60`, `RIGHT_X = 520`,
  `HANGAR_ROW_STEP = 16`) plus four fixed bottom rows
  (`HANGAR_BUILDOUT_ROW_Y`, `HANGAR_RESTART_ROW_Y`, `HANGAR_MAP_ROW_Y`,
  `HANGAR_DEPLOY_ROW_Y`) and an unframed `TARGET INTEL` block top-left. Headings
  are plain 13px monospace text via the local `heading()` helper; there is no
  frame, no section rect table and no detail surface.
- Rows are labelled today as `<name> — <price> — <action>` (unlocks) and
  `HULL <name> [— EQUIPPED]`, `LOADOUT <name> [— EQUIPPED]`,
  `MODIFIER <name> — ON|OFF` (selector); the catalogue `description` field
  exists on every entry but is never read by the screen.
- `hangarRightColumnLayout()` derives the right column's Ys from row counts and
  `HangarScene.test.ts` pins them (`hangarLowestRowY(model) <
  HANGAR_RESTART_ROW_Y`), so the layout is already single-sourced for the game
  and the gym.
- `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) already registers every
  actionable row and drives `tab`/arrow movement; the renderer currently reads
  it only for the restart disarm check — there is no focus-change callback yet.
- The hex map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) is the design-language
  reference: `HEX_MAP_SECTION_RECTS` (one `{x,y,width,height}` per section),
  `drawSectionPanel` (`SECTION_FILL` 0x03131c @ 0.35, hairline `SECTION_LINE`
  0x1f4a5a @ 0.9, 4px rounded, 10px monospace `HEADING_COLOR` heading),
  `wrappedLineCount`/`sectionBudgetHeight` for canvas-free height budgeting, and
  a `sections` registry published on `HexMapView` (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM,
  AH-0MWL8N8CH0040JWL).
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` already carries everything the panel needs:
  `description` per entry, hull `baseDefence`/`upgrades`/`runStats`/`skill`,
  weapon `weaponId`, modifier `effect` (`extra-lives` | `defence` |
  `defence-skill`), `minRing`, `price`, `starter`.
- `GymHangar` (`src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts`) renders the same model read-only
  with no handlers; `GymHangar.test.ts` asserts model equality with the game.

## Desired change

1. Extend the pure model with the detail content: a
   `buildHangarDetail(screenModel, key)` (or an equivalent pure builder) that
   returns, for any focusable row key, a heading plus body lines — the
   catalogue description, the kind-specific facts, the economy's price/state
   verdicts and, for the no-focus fallback, the deployment summary from
   `buildHangarDeployment`. Unit-tested as a table over every row kind and every
   unlock state (`owned`, `buyable`, `gated`, `unaffordable`, `upgradable`,
   `upgrade-unaffordable`, `capped`, plus `blocked` power-ups and the saved-build
   verbs).
2. Re-lay the screen out as framed sections with a single-source rect table
   (e.g. `HANGAR_SECTION_RECTS`) published on `HangarScreenView.sections`, with
   the detail panel between the unlock tree and the deployment selector, and the
   fixed rows inside a framed actions block. Rect heights derived from the
   model's row counts, pinned by the non-overlap / row-fit / in-frame tests.
3. Wire focus to the panel: every registered row reports its focus (and pointer
   enter) so the centre panel follows the focused row, falling back to the
   deployment summary when nothing is focused; the restart disarm-on-focus-move
   behaviour must keep working through the same seam.
4. Share the panel style with the hex map (extract the frame/padding/colour
   constants and `drawSectionPanel` into a neutral shared module) so both
   screens draw the same panel; the hex map's rendering stays byte-identical
   (its existing tests pin it).
5. Update the module docblock, GDD §8.2's hangar-screen description and
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and extend the gym parity assertion to the new sections
   and detail content.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — new pure detail builder, section
  rect table, framed renderer, focus→detail wiring; row labels shorten to fit
  three columns.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/sectionPanel.ts` *(new)* — shared frame/padding/colour
  constants + `drawSectionPanel` extracted from `hexMap.ts`, consumed by the
  hangar screen and the hex map.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — consumes the extracted shared panel
  helpers; rendering unchanged (existing tests keep pinning it).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.detail.test.ts` *(new)* — table tests for
  the detail builder across every row kind/state and the deployment fallback.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — layout invariants (in-frame, non-overlap,
  row-inside-section, row-fit) and focus→detail behaviour.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — nothing rule-bearing; may need no change beyond
  the focus callback wiring if it lives in the view.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — read-only
  parity for the new sections and detail panel.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — read-only source of descriptions/effects
  (no change expected; a missing description would be a catalogue gap).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2) — record the
  hangar screen's framed sections and centre detail panel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Row-width regression (highest risk).** Three columns at 13px monospace can
  no longer hold `RICHOCHET — LV 1/3 — UPGRADE · 60 min — NEED 40 min`. Mitigated
  by shortening row labels to a state chip and moving the long form into the
  panel, with a row-fit test at worst case; if a column still cannot fit, reduce
  the selector column's type size (never below the map's 9px floor) rather than
  overlapping.
- **Height budget.** Full catalogue + full loadout + saved builds is the tall
  case; a centre panel does not add height, but framed padding and headings do.
  Mitigated by deriving rects from row counts and pinning `hangarLowestRowY`
  against the actions block.
- **Divergence risk in the shared panel extraction.** Moving
  `drawSectionPanel` out of `hexMap.ts` touches a shipped screen; the hex map's
  existing budget/rect/rendering tests are the regression gate and must stay
  green without being weakened.
- **Two sources of matchup truth.** The detail panel repeats a row's
  `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` verdict; it must read the row's own model field,
  never re-resolve the matchup (AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y is an open item about when
  that mark is appropriate — this item must not pre-empt its decision).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Adjacent wants — explaining *why* the suggested buildout
  picks an option, per-hull comparison tables, hover tooltips, a scrollable
  catalogue — are **out of scope**; record them as follow-up work items rather
  than absorbing them here.
- **Assumption:** the detail panel is driven by focus (keyboard and pointer),
  not a separate cursor, because the hex map's `SELECTED HEX` panel already
  works that way and the producer's wording is "the currently selected option".
- **Assumption:** detail content is limited to data the repo already ships
  (catalogue `description`, structured stats/effects, economy verdicts). No new
  balance numbers are authored here.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM — Hex Map Information UX** (completed): the design
  language being reused — framed, headed, bounded sections plus a published
  section registry.
- **AH-0MWL8N8CH0040JWL — Sections registry on `HexMapView` + scene/gym query
  seam** (completed): the `sections` publication pattern to mirror on
  `HangarScreenView`.
- **AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 — Target intel and matchup marks** (completed): added
  the unframed `TARGET INTEL` block and per-row matchup marks this item reframes.
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7 — Saved ship configurations** (completed): the
  fixed-height `SAVED BUILDS` surface and its dense rows, which the detail panel
  must also describe.
- **AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDHH — Buy-to-upgrade rows** (completed): the
  `LV n/MAX` + priced-upgrade row affordance whose long form moves into the panel.
- **AH-0MWOWEPO2004B0MR / AH-0MWOWEYZQ006IR9T — auto-fit loadout and
  `⚡ APPLY SUGGESTED BUILDOUT`** (completed): behaviour that must be preserved
  exactly, and the natural home of the "why this suggestion" follow-up.
- **AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y — Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading** (open):
  owns when a matchup mark should be shown; this item must display the row's
  verdict verbatim and pre-empt nothing.
- **AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3 — `⟲ RESTART WAR` two-step confirm** (completed): the
  disarm-on-focus-move behaviour that the new focus→detail seam must preserve.
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1 — Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout
  selector** (completed): the screen this item relayouts; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
  binds it and `GymHangar` to one code path.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9 — Text on hex map is unreadable** (completed): the
  readability precedent (tile text size floor, detail in a panel) that the
  three-column row-fit constraint follows.
- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the
  hold-full choice list** (completed): prior art for surfacing "what changes if
  I pick this" beside a choice list.
- **AH-0MWW5FW4Y009GNBN — Improve language on win/defeat screen** (open):
  unrelated screen, shared UX-writing concern (plain-language option text); no
  code overlap, listed for the automated related-work sweep only.
- **Automated find-related sweep** (this item): 3 related work items above and
  3 repository matches (`README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/BALANCING.md`) — the GDD is the documentation of record updated under
  the ACs; the other two matches are keyword-only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What selects the option the centre panel describes — keyboard focus,
  mouse hover, or a separate cursor?"
  Answer (intake, documented assumption, no producer available in this run —
  plausible from repo evidence): focus-driven, following both keyboard focus
  and pointer hover, with the deployment summary as the no-focus fallback.
  Research: `src/utils/focusManager.ts` already tracks the focused row and the
  hex map's `SELECTED HEX` panel is focus-driven (`hexMap.ts` module docblock
  "focused hex's full known-ahead intel renders in the `selected-hex`
  section"); the item title says "currently selected option". Producer may
  overrule at review.
- Q: "How much detail — the data already shipped, or newly authored stat sheets
  / comparison data?"
  Answer (intake, documented assumption): shipped data only — catalogue
  `description`, hull `baseDefence`/`upgrades`/`runStats`/`skill`, modifier
  `effect`, power-up level/cap/blocked state, economy price/state verdicts and
  matchup mark. Research: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` carries all of it (the
  `description` field is currently rendered nowhere); authoring new balance
  numbers would be a rules change needing its own item. Producer may overrule
  at review.
- Q: "May existing row labels get shorter to make room for three columns?"
  Answer (intake, documented assumption): yes — the long form moves into the
  detail panel, pinned by a row-fit test at worst-case width. Research: the
  tallest current labels are ~50 monospace characters and three columns at
  960px cannot hold them beside the new panel.
  Producer may overrule at review.
- Q: "Should the panel also explain why `⚡ APPLY SUGGESTED BUILDOUT` picks what
  it picks?"
  Answer (intake): OPEN QUESTION, non-blocking — recorded as a scope-creep risk
  and a candidate follow-up item rather than absorbed into this one.

data.description:
# Randomize the hex war starter weapon

## Problem statement

The Hangar War ("hex war") fleet always begins a war with the same free
starter weapon — the Spread Cannon (`spread`, `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`), authored in
the hangar catalogue as the `starter: true` entry and seeded into every fresh
payload's `unlockedWeapons`. The first battle therefore always flies the same
gun. The producer wants the starter weapon randomised from the ring-1 weapons
in the catalogue, free and auto-equipped for the very first battle.

## Users

- **The returning hangar-war player** — "A fresh war should feel like a
  different starting hand, not the same Spread Cannon every reset."
- **The first-time hangar-war player** — "The very first battle should start me
  with one of the catalogue's weapons, already fitted, at no cost."
- **The maintainer** — "The draw must be deterministic for the war seed and
  must never let the player lose the starter (no soft-lock)."

User stories:

- As a player, when I start a new war (or restart one), I want the very first
  battle to be equipped with a randomly chosen ring-1 weapon at no cost, so
  each war opens with a different kit.
- As a player, I want the randomised starter to remain owned and free through
  that war, including after a battle I flew it in, so I can never be left with
  no weapon.
- As a player with an existing save, I want my current starter and loadout left
  exactly as they are, so the change does not rewrite my war.

## Acceptance Criteria

> Answers recorded from the producer on 2026-11-25 (Appendix Q1–Q3): the
> randomised thing is **the weapon available in the very first battle, at no
> cost**; the draw pool is **all ring-1 weapons**, and the drawn weapon is
> **free**; the starter is **auto-equipped**.

- A **fresh war** (`createDefaultPayload(<seed>)` or a first load with no save)
  draws one starter from **every purchasable ring-1 weapon** in the hangar
  catalogue (`kind === 'weapon'`, `minRing <= 1`, `isPurchasableEntry`) and
  **auto-equips** it in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, so the very first
  deployment (`buildHangarDeployment`) carries it as a starting weapon. The draw
  is **deterministic for the payload seed** (the same seed always yields the
  same starter; different seeds can yield different starters, and a seeded
  sweep shows every eligible entry is reachable). The drawn starter costs
  nothing — no minerals or cores are deducted, even when its catalogue price is
  non-zero.
- A **restart** (`restartHangarWar`, which supplies a fresh random seed)
  re-draws the starter with that fresh seed and auto-equips it, while still
  preserving `bestScore` and saved builds and returning the rest of the hangar
  to its documented starting kit (zero salvage, ring 1, no queued attacks).
- The randomised starter is **owned and free for that war**, is never
  consumed by `consumeDeployedShip` on **win or loss**, and is protected
  exactly as today's `spread` starter is — so no battle outcome can leave the
  fleet without a free weapon (no soft-lock). Its permanent level rows follow
  the existing starter rules.
- **Existing saves are unchanged**: a stored payload keeps its current owned
  starter, loadout and hangar state (no re-roll on load, no loadout rewrite, no
  back-fill). Migration stays field-presence based, no schema version bump is
  required, and a legacy save's implicit starter remains `spread`; a legacy
  save's empty loadout is still filled by the existing hangar auto-fit on open,
  not by this change.
- Regression coverage is added/updated for: seeded determinism and ring-1
  eligibility, the auto-equipped first deployment, no-cost acquisition, starter
  survival through win **and** loss consumption, a legacy-save round-trip with
  no re-roll, the restart re-draw, the attract/traversal bot invariance and the
  `GymHexWar`/`GymHangar` parity path — with the existing pinned expectations
  that hard-code `spread` as the starter updated deliberately (red-first where
  the behaviour changes).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically
  the GDD's Hangar War starting-kit, empty-loadout and auto-fit sections (the
  documented "starter never auto-equips" rule is superseded for a fresh war's
  first deployment), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` wherever the starter appears, and the
  affected module docblocks.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The very first Hangar War battle now flies a randomly chosen ring-1 weapon at
no cost — seeded per war and already auto-equipped — instead of always the
Spread Cannon, while an existing save keeps the starter and loadout it already
has.

## Constraints

- **Draw pool.** Every purchasable ring-1 weapon entry in the hangar catalogue,
  including `spread` itself; grant-only entries (`GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`) and
  non-weapon kinds are excluded. The draw iterates the catalogue, never a
  hard-coded four, so AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 grows the pool without another
  change.
- **Auto-equip supersedes AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D for a fresh war only.** The
  initial loadout is no longer empty for a new war; the post-battle reset still
  empties the loadout and the hangar auto-fit still fills an empty one, and an
  existing save's loadout is never rewritten. The GDD's empty-loadout and
  starter-never-auto-equips notes must be updated accordingly.
- **No cost.** The draw must not deduct minerals or cores; a drawn paid weapon
  is free only as the war's starter, and its normal price and ring gate remain
  for any future purchase.
- **No soft-lock.** The war's starter must be owned and protected from
  `consumeDeployedShip` on win and loss (the protection must key off the war's
  starter id, not the fixed `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`).
- **Determinism.** Randomness must come from the existing seeded hangar-war RNG
  (`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`) derived from the war seed — no unseeded
  `Math.random()` — so replays, traversal tests and the parity harness stay
  deterministic.
- **Attract/traversal bot invariance.** If the unpicked default `spread`
  becomes an unowned zero-price entry, the bot's cheapest-useful-unlock rule
  must not start buying it: keep its decisions, seeded replays and pinned
  unlock pace byte-identical (e.g. exclude zero-price entries from the bot's
  candidate gate, a no-op today) and prove it with the existing traversal
  tests.
- **Migration.** The versioned payload's field-presence policy holds: an
  additive per-war starter field (or an equivalent seed-derived record), no
  schema bump, and old saves keep `spread`.
- Balance is otherwise untouched: no drawn ring-2/gated weapon, no change to
  salvage, prices or the ring model.
- CHANGELOG.md is handled by the ship/release pipeline — do not edit it.

## Existing state

- `STARTER_WEAPON_ID = 'spread'` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) and the
  catalogue entry `{ id: 'spread', starter: true, price: { minerals: 0, cores: 0 } }`
  designate the one free starter weapon.
- `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID = 'spread'` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`)
  seeds `createDefaultPayload(...).hangar.unlockedWeapons`, and the fresh
  payload's `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` is empty.
- `ownsEntry` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) returns true for every
  `entry.starter`, so `spread` is owned regardless of the payload's sets.
- `consumeDeployedShip` protects `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` and resets the active
  loadout to empty after every hex battle.
- `restartHangarWar` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) builds a fresh
  payload from a fresh random seed (`randomSeed()`), preserving `bestScore` and
  saved builds.
- The hangar auto-fit (`isDefaultHangarLoadout` / boss-aware suggestion) fills
  an empty loadout on open, so today the owned starter is what a first war
  flies after the screen is opened; a deployment without opening the hangar
  carries only the permanent cannon.
- `HANGAR_FALLBACK_WEAPON_ID = STARTER_WEAPON_ID` is the hangar screen's
  fallback pointer.
- The catalogue's weapon list is currently four entries (`spread`,
  `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster`), all `minRing: 1`; AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91
  will derive one entry per `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` weapon, so the pool grows.
- The attract/traversal bot's `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (pure economy) and
  `cheapestSeededUnlock` (`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) both gate through
  `isBotPurchaseCandidate`; today `spread` is starter-owned, so its zero price
  never enters the comparison.
- `hangarEconomy.test.ts` pins `STARTER_WEAPON_ID === DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`;
  several store, screen, gym and integration suites hard-code `spread` as the
  starter.

## Desired change

A fresh war draws its starter from every purchasable ring-1 weapon in the
hangar catalogue using the war's seeded hangar-war RNG, records it as the war's
starter, owns it at no cost and auto-equips it in the initial loadout so the
very first deployment flies it. The starter is protected from win/loss
consumption; restarting re-draws with the fresh seed; existing saves keep their
current starter and loadout. The catalogue's fixed `starter: true` ownership is
replaced by the per-war starter (with `spread` as the legacy fallback for old
saves), the attract bot's candidate rule is kept unchanged, and the GDD and
parity docs are updated.

**Key Files:**

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`, the `starter: true`
  weapon entry and the ring-1 weapon list: the starter designation becomes
  per-war (or the weapon list is exposed as the draw pool).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`,
  `createDefaultPayload` (draw, record and auto-equip the starter), `parseHangar`
  (legacy saves keep `spread`; additive field if used).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `ownsEntry` (starter ownership),
  `consumeDeployedShip` (protect the war's starter),
  `resolveActiveLoadout`/`ownedEntriesOf`, and the bot's candidate gate.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — the seeded `pick` used for the draw.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `restartHangarWar` re-draw,
  `HANGAR_FALLBACK_WEAPON_ID`, and the FREE/owned unlock row.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — deployment resolution and the
  auto-fit consumers.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` — the traversal bot's shared candidate gate
  (invariance guard).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar*.test.ts` — pinned `spread` starter expectations.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§ Hangar War starting kit / empty-loadout /
  auto-fit) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the starter rule.

## Risks and mitigations

- **A free drawn ring-gated weapon undermines the unlock tree** → the pool is
  ring-1 purchasable weapons only; free only as that war's starter; its normal
  price and ring gate remain for purchase.
- **Soft-lock if the starter is consumed** → the war's starter is owned and
  protected in `consumeDeployedShip`; no battle outcome removes it.
- **The bot starts buying the now-unowned zero-price `spread`** → the shared
  `isBotPurchaseCandidate` gate must exclude zero-price entries (a no-op today)
  or the traversal/unlock-pace tests must prove the decision stream unchanged.
- **Non-determinism breaks replays and parity** → seeded draw through
  `createHangarWarRng`; a same-seed test plus the gym parity suites cover it.
- **Auto-equip contradicts a documented rule** → the GDD and the
  AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D note are updated in the same change; legacy saves are
  explicitly not rewritten.
- **Scope creep into the catalogue-derivation item** → AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91
  stays separate; this change iterates whatever the catalogue holds.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons
  in the loadout (default weapon only): the empty-loadout default this change
  supersedes for a fresh war's first deployment, and the rule it must preserve
  for legacy saves.
- **AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91** — Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon
  entries from weapons.csv: grows the catalogue's ring-1 weapon list, which is
  the random draw pool.
- **AH-0MWW5RACR000UCKU** — Maintain weapon Lvl between losses: touches
  `consumeDeployedShip`, whose starter protection this change must respect.
- **AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3** — Hangar War needs a restart button: the restart
  already supplies a fresh random seed, which makes the per-restart re-draw
  natural.
- **AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD** — Automatically select strong weapons: the
  empty-loadout auto-fit that remains the path for a legacy save's empty
  loadout.
- **AH-0MWLE90B30013MPZ** — War reset preserves saved builds: the reset
  contract the re-draw must not disturb.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D (Hangar War) design of record;
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar War.

## Assumptions (documented, reversible)

- **A1 — routine:** "the catalogue" is the hangar catalogue (`HANGAR_CATALOGUE`),
  the one authored weapon list the game consumes; the full `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`
  is reached through it (AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91).
- **A2 — routine:** the draw is per **war**, not per deployment — the war seed
  identifies a fresh war and `restartHangarWar` re-seeds — so no per-battle
  randomness or new persisted state is needed.
- **A3 — routine:** existing saves are not rewritten — no re-roll on load and
  no back-fill; they keep whatever starter and loadout they own today.
- **A4 — routine:** the draw is seeded through `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`, so
  the same seed always yields the same starter (replay and parity tests).
- **A5 — producer answers (2026-11-25):** Q1 = the weapon available in the very
  first battle at no cost; Q2 = all ring-1 weapons, free; Q3 = auto-equip.
  These are the design of record for this item.
- **A6 — routine:** the drawn starter is recorded on the hangar (e.g. an
  additive per-war `starterWeaponId`, or an equivalent seed-derived record) and
  owned for that war; `spread` remains the legacy fallback for a save that
  predates the field. Planning chooses the exact record.
- **A7 — routine:** the draw pool includes `spread` itself (it is a purchasable
  ring-1 weapon), so a fresh war can still start with the Spread Cannon by
  chance; "randomised" does not mean "never spread".
- **A8 — routine:** after a battle the existing reset and hangar auto-fit rules
  apply; only the fresh war's initial loadout is auto-equipped by this change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Which "starter weapon" is being randomised? (answered)

The item's wording could mean two different things:

- (a) the **free starter weapon the fleet owns** from its first deployment —
  today `spread` (Spread Cannon), owned but not equipped; or
- (b) the **weapon a hex deployment actually flies** — today an empty default
  loadout resolves to the ship's permanent cannon, and the hangar's auto-fit is
  the only thing that fills it.

**Recommended:** (a) — it is the only fixed "starter weapon" in the Hangar
War, matches the catalogue's `starter: true` entry, and (b) would contradict
the documented empty-loadout rule AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "The weapon that is available in the very
first battle, at no cost." — the randomised starter is the weapon the **first
battle** carries, drawn free; combined with Q3 it is auto-equipped. Source:
interactive reply.

### Q2 — Which weapons are eligible, and is the drawn starter free? (answered)

- (a) every weapon entry in the hangar catalogue, free for that war;
- (b) only weapons reachable at ring 1 / already unlockable, free;
- (c) every catalogue weapon, but at its normal price (the "starter" is only
  the owned entry, not a free one).

**Recommended:** (a) — "available weapons in the catalogue" reads as the full
weapon list, and "starter" implies free; ring gating still governs purchase, so
a drawn ring-2 weapon is free as the starter but not buyable.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "all ring 1, and yes, free" — the draw pool
is every ring-1 purchasable weapon, and the drawn starter costs nothing.
Source: interactive reply.

### Q3 — Should the randomised starter be equipped for the first deployment? (answered)

- (a) no — keep the documented "starter never auto-equips" rule; the starter
  stays owned and the hangar's auto-fit puts it into the first run;
- (b) yes — a fresh war's `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` starts with the drawn
  starter so the first deployment flies it immediately.

**Recommended:** (a) — preserves AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D and the
starter-never-auto-equips rule; (b) changes a documented producer decision.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "auto-equip" — the fresh war's initial
loadout carries the drawn starter so the first deployment flies it. Source:
interactive reply. This supersedes the empty-loadout default and the
starter-never-auto-equips rule **for a fresh war only**; legacy saves are not
rewritten.

### R1 — Duplicate check (routine, answered)

No completed item already satisfies this request. Closest completed work is
AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with no extra weapons — the default
loadout), AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD (auto-fit strong weapons) and AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3
(restart with a fresh seed); none randomises the starter weapon.
AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 is related future work (grows the weapon pool), not a
duplicate. Source: `wl search "hex war starter weapon"`, `wl search "random
starter"`, `wl search "starting weapon catalogue"`.

### R2 — Randomness source (routine, answered)

The war already carries a seeded stream (`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`,
`createHangarWarRng(seed)` with `pick`), derived from the payload's seed, and
`restartHangarWar` supplies a fresh `randomSeed()`. Using it keeps every
replay, traversal and parity harness deterministic. Research: inspected
`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`
(`restartHangarWar`), `src/core/rng.ts`.

### R3 — Migration policy (routine, answered)

The versioned hangar-war payload migrates by field presence; old saves must
keep their current starter. `parseHangar` does not force a starter weapon into
`unlockedWeapons` today (only the hull is forced), so an old save's owned
starter is whatever it stored. Research: inspected `parseHangar` in
`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` and `docs/Game Design Document.md`
§ `ai_hell_hangar_war`.

### R4 — Attract-bot impact (routine, answered)

If `spread` stops being starter-owned, its zero-price entry would become the
bot's cheapest useful unlock and change the seeded traversal/unlock pace
(pinned by the AH-0MWKT12BT001106T tests). The shared `isBotPurchaseCandidate`
gate is the one place both bot consumers read; excluding zero-price entries
there is a no-op today (the only free entry is starter-owned) and keeps the
demo unchanged. Research: inspected `cheapestUsefulUnlock`
(`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`), `cheapestSeededUnlock`
(`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) and `isBotPurchaseCandidate`
(`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`).

## Plan (features and implementation tasks)

Phasing: one tracer bullet cut into vertical slices — every child lands code,
tests and the docblock it touches together, so the tree is never left half
wired. The item is Small (~19 h recommended), so no horizontal phases; the
children are executed in the dependency order below.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AH-0MWWM4YSH00078CI — Test: randomised starter weapon contract (test-first) | task | — | AC1 (pool + determinism), AC5 (red-first contract) |

### Agreed contract (implementation must follow; child 1 pins it)

  `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)`, `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)` and

  - Pool = `kind === 'weapon'` && `minRing <= 1` && `isPurchasableEntry(entry)`;
    iterates the catalogue, so AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 grows it with no change here.
  - Draw = `createHangarWarRng(seed).pick(pool)` — no `Math.random()`.
  - Resolve = `hangar.starterWeaponId` when present, else the legacy
    `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` (`spread`); a corrupt/unknown id falls back to the legacy

# Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard (test-first verification)

## Goal

*As a balancing agent, I want a measured, allocation-bounded budget for the
enemy-bullet advance **before** the Chrono field gains a per-bullet check, so the
range-limited slow cannot silently regress frame time.*

This is the plan's **test/verification first** slice: it adds only tests plus a
`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` note, changes no production behaviour, and is green on
arrival. It pins the cost budget that the per-bullet check
([Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms]) must meet.

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3 (Chrono Field nerfing), constraint
  "Performance — membership must be a squared-distance compare with no per-bullet
  allocation and no new per-frame garbage".
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts:87` `advanceWrappingBullets` is the single
  per-frame enemy-bullet hot loop (game + every gym).
- Precedent for the assertion style: AH-0MVXV0F0Y004NENT (per-frame allocation
  removal) and the hot-loop guards it added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` gains an allocation-budget test that advances a large array (≥500 bullets) through `advanceWrappingBullets` over many frames and asserts the hot loop creates no new arrays/objects per bullet (bounded heap growth, same measurement technique as the AH-0MVXV0F0Y004NENT guards).
- The test asserts a documented, stable per-frame cost budget for the current uniform-`dt` advance and fails loudly if a future change exceeds it (the number and its meaning are recorded in the test's doc comment).
- The guard is green on today's code and this item changes no production behaviour (no source edit outside tests and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`).
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` gains a one-line note that the enemy-bullet advance carries a documented allocation/cost budget enforced by this test, naming the test.
- **Parent AC9 closed by this item** — **Tests** — new/updated unit tests cover the slow curve (level 0, mid-level, cap), the radius curve, the membership maths (inside, outside, exactly on the boundary) and the active/inactive window; scene-level tests prove an inside bullet is slowed while an outside bullet is not, in the game and in each affected gym; the ring's drawn/cleared lifecycle is tested. **Full project test suite must pass** with the change (run through the test skill, never ad-hoc invocations).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` with the allocation-budget + baseline-cost test (reusing the existing allocation-guard idiom, no new harness).
- Add the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` pointer line.
- No production code change.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — the new budget test.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — the budget note.
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — read only (the measured seam).

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice and unblocks the sizing evidence for
`Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms`.

# Shared per-bullet time-scale seam

## Goal

*As an agent / gym user, I want the enemy-bullet advance to accept a per-bullet
time scale, so Chrono can slow only the bullets inside its field through one
shared implementation that the game and every gym run identically.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, constraint "**Shared-core discipline** — the
  per-bullet slowed dt belongs in `src/scenes/core/` (an optional per-bullet
  time-scale hook on `advanceWrappingBullets`) and every consumer passes the same
  resolver" and "**Backwards-compatible helper** — the per-bullet scale must be
  optional with today's uniform-dt behaviour as the default".
- Today's call sites: `PlayScene._advanceBullets` (~:5215),
  `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` (~:2183), `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690, currently raw `dt`).
- Adjacent, not in scope: **AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB — World slow-motion time scale**
  (blocked) must be able to compose its `teleportTimeScale()` multiplicatively
  with this seam; a pure, side-effect-free resolver keeps that possible. Do not
  implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `advanceWrappingBullets` accepts an **optional** per-bullet time-scale resolver (e.g. a trailing `resolveScale?: (bullet: T) => number` parameter); omitting it reproduces today's uniform-`dt` behaviour exactly, so every existing caller and test passes unchanged.
- With a resolver supplied, each bullet integrates position, ages `elapsed`, fades and expires on **its own** scaled dt inside a single call — two bullets in one call advance by different distances — so no scene can apply a scale twice.
- The resolver is consulted exactly once per bullet per call, using the bullet's pre-integration position, and the loop introduces no closure, array or object allocation per bullet (satisfied against the `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` budget test).
- Player bullets are untouched: `advancePlayerBullets` keeps its signature and behaviour, and a test asserts a Chrono-style resolver never reaches player bullets.
- The helper remains a **single** definition in `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard is extended if a new exported resolver helper appears, and it passes.
- The helper's doc comment states this is the one seam every scene uses for enemy-bullet time scaling (and the composition point for future world slow-motion).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the optional resolver parameter to `advanceWrappingBullets` and use `dt * scale` for ageing, integration, fade and expiry (one scale read per bullet, no allocation).
- Tests first: default path unchanged, per-bullet divergence, once-per-call invocation, ageing/fade coupling, player-bullet exclusion.
- Extend the equivalence guard's symbol list if a new exported helper is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — the seam (one definition).
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — the new behavioural tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body / shared-symbol guard.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` (the budget this seam must respect).

# Halve Chrono slow, add radius axis

## Goal

*As a designer, I want the Chrono slow halved and a level-scaled field radius in
the committed level catalogue, so the nerf's numbers are inspectable and a future
rebalance cannot silently restore the old potency.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, producer decisions **Q1 = B** (ship-centred circle
  whose radius grows with the level) and **Q3 = A** (halve the whole slow axis).
- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (~:953) is the
  single source; `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` resolves it;
  `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` (~:1574) derives level-up copy from the specs, so
  a new axis appears in the copy automatically.
- Target numbers: `chronoSlowFactor` 0.25 → 0.375 (`k = 0.25` unchanged);
  `chronoRadius` 150 px → 300 px (`k = 0.12`), i.e. 167 / 218 / 255 px at levels
  1 / 5 / 10. `enemyBulletTimeScale()` therefore reads 0.75 at level 0 and 0.625 at
  the cap.
- No CSV/config rows: the catalogue is the source of truth (parent assumption A7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono`'s `chronoSlowFactor` entry is `base 0.25` → `cap 0.375` on the unchanged `k = 0.25` exponential-saturation curve, with its label, description and rationale updated to describe the nerfed field.
- `chronoRadius` is added as a `PowerUpLevelVariable` (union member with a doc comment), to `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` immediately after `chronoSlowFactor`, to `PowerUpLevelStats`, and as a spec entry in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` with label, unit `px`, description, rationale and exponential-saturation `base 150` → `cap 300`, `k = 0.12`.
- `resolvePowerUpAtLevel('chrono', level)` reports both axes; unit tests pin the slow at levels 0 / 1 / 5 / 10 / cap (0.25 / 0.278 / 0.339 / 0.365 / 0.375) and the radius at levels 0 / 1 / 5 / 10 / cap (150 / 167 / 218 / 255 / 300) within a documented tolerance.
- `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` stays empty and the existing catalogue-order, curve-shape and deferred-set tests pass with the new axis present.
- While the Chrono window is active `EffectsRegistry.enemyBulletTimeScale()` reports 0.75 at level 0 and 0.625 at the cap (0.722 / 0.661 / 0.635 at levels 1 / 5 / 10) and exactly 1 when inactive; `summarisePowerUpLevelChange('chrono', n, n + 1)` reports the radius delta alongside the slow and duration deltas.
- `EffectsRegistry` exposes a level-resolved `chronoFieldRadius()` beside `forceFieldRadius()` reading the same catalogue value, as the **single radius source** for the membership test, the ring and the copy (returns the resolved radius; the window gate stays with the caller).
- **Parent AC1 closed by this item** — **Halved potency at every level** — while the Chrono window is active the level-resolved `chronoSlowFactor` is `base 0.25` → `cap 0.375` on the unchanged `k = 0.25` curve, so `enemyBulletTimeScale()` reports **0.75** at level 0 and **0.625** at the cap (and 0.722 / 0.661 / 0.635 at levels 1 / 5 / 10), replacing today's 0.5 → 0.25; unit tests pin the level-0 and cap values.
- **Parent AC2 closed by this item** — **New level-scaled radius axis** — `chronoRadius` is added to `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` (in catalogue order beside `chronoSlowFactor` and `chronoDuration`), `PowerUpLevelStats` and `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` with a label, unit (`px`) and rationale, resolving `base 150 px → cap 300 px` on exponential-saturation `k = 0.12`; the registry exposes it, the deferred-variable set stays empty, the catalogue-order/curve-shape tests pass, and level-up change summaries report the radius delta.

## Minimal implementation

- Halve the `chronoSlowFactor` base/cap and rewrite its rationale.
- Add the `chronoRadius` axis end-to-end through the catalogue (union, ordered list, stats interface, spec).
- Add `chronoFieldRadius()` to the registry; update `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts` and the parity tests that read Chrono values.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — the catalogue (single source of truth).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `enemyBulletTimeScale()` doc/value and the new `chronoFieldRadius()`.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — curve, order, deferred and copy tests.
- `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts` — the Chrono effect assertions.

## Dependencies

None — independent of the shared seam; it unblocks
`Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms` and `Draw the Chrono active-field ring`.

# Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms

## Goal

*As a player, I want Chrono to slow only the bullets near my ship, so the field is
a positional dodge aid I have to fly into rather than a screen-wide brake.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, producer decisions **Q1 = B** (ship-centred,
  level-scaled radius) and **A3** (inclusive boundary, matching
  `dangerDetection.isWithinRadiusSq`: `dx² + dy² <= radiusSq`).
- Replaces the single global scalar (today `dt * enemyBulletTimeScale()` at
  `PlayScene.ts:5215` and `GymFormationScene.ts:2183`, and **no scale at all** in
  `GymPowerUpsCombat` ~:690 — a pre-existing parity gap this item closes).
- Inclusive-boundary precedent: `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts:37`
  `isWithinRadiusSq`.
- Adjacent, not in scope: AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB (world slow-motion) must be able to
  multiply its own scale into this seam later — keep the resolver pure and
  composable; do not implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure, hot-loop-safe membership resolver in `src/scenes/core/` returns the slowed scale when a bullet's squared distance from the **player ship** is `<= radiusSq` (inclusive: a bullet exactly on the radius counts as inside) and exactly `1.0` outside, with no allocation, no per-bullet closure and no easing or hysteresis at the boundary; unit tests cover inside, outside and exactly-on-the-boundary.
- `PlayScene._advanceBullets` passes the per-bullet resolver, anchored on `this.player`, through the shared seam; a scene test proves one inside bullet advances at the slowed step while an outside bullet advances at exactly `dt` in the same frame, at level 0 and at the cap.
- `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` uses the identical resolver and radius (inherited by every formation gym) with no duplicated body, and its test proves the same inside/outside behaviour.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._advanceEnemyBullets` now runs the same seam (closing its pre-existing "no Chrono scale" divergence), and its test proves inside-slow / outside-normal.
- Membership is re-evaluated every frame from current positions: a test moves a bullet from outside to inside and back and proves the step changes on that frame with no sticky or accumulated scale and no double application; a slowed bullet's lifetime/fade still stretch exactly as today (ageing on the scaled dt).
- The resolver stays composable with a multiplicative outer time scale (so AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB needs no rewrite), `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard passes naming the new shared resolver, and `gymParityDocs.test.ts` passes.
- **Parent AC3 closed by this item** — **Range-limited slow** — only enemy bullets whose position lies **inside** the current radius (measured from the **player ship**, inclusive boundary: a bullet exactly on the radius counts as inside) are slowed; every enemy bullet outside advances at exactly **1.0×** normal speed. Verified in the game **and** in each gym that advances enemy bullets (AC5).
- **Parent AC4 closed by this item** — **Per-frame re-evaluation** — membership is computed from each bullet's current position every frame: a bullet entering or leaving the field changes speed on that frame, with no accumulated or sticky scale, no double-application, and no change to lifetime/fade accounting beyond the slowed ageing the effect already applies (a slowed bullet still ages on the scaled dt, so its lifetime stretches exactly as today).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the pure resolver (squared-distance compare, one call per bullet) to the shared core next to the bullet-lifecycle seam.
- Wire `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` to it, anchored on each scene's player.
- Tests first: resolver unit tests (inside/outside/boundary/per-frame), then the three scene tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/` — the new shared membership resolver beside `bulletLifecycle.ts`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_advanceBullets` ~:5215), `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (~:8552).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:2183) and its test.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690) and its test.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts` (:338) — the existing Chrono-effect assertion may need updating.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Shared per-bullet time-scale seam` (the hook this wiring consumes).
- Blocked by `Halve Chrono slow, add radius axis` (the radius and slow values it reads).

## Goal

*As a player, I want to see the slowed zone as a ring around my ship, so I can

  ~:1389, `GymPowerUpsCombat`'s equivalents ~:594).
- One radius source: `EffectsRegistry.chronoFieldRadius()` (added by
  `Halve Chrono slow, add radius axis`); never a duplicated constant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `CombatEffectVisuals` gains a `drawChronoFieldRing` helper beside the existing bubble/aura helpers that draws a ship-centred ring of exactly `registry.chronoFieldRadius()` while the Chrono window is active, and clears it (returning `false`) when the window is inactive or the graphics/player is missing.
- A test asserts the drawn radius equals the registry value at level 0 and at the cap, so the visual can never disagree with the effect, and that the helper allocates no new objects per frame (it reuses the scene-owned Graphics like the other auras).
- The ring is visually distinguishable from the Shield bubble, Force Field bubble (hexagon) and Thorn aura (spiked halo): its own documented colour/width constants beside `FORCE_FIELD_COLOR`, with a rationale comment (e.g. a thin dashed/segmented circle in a Chrono-specific hue).
- `PlayScene._updateVisuals`, `GymFormationScene._updateEffectVisuals` and `GymPowerUpsCombat`'s effect-visual dispatch all draw it through the one shared helper, each owning its Graphics object created and torn down like the existing aura graphics.
- A lifecycle test proves the ring is drawn while the window is active, cleared the frame the window expires, and cleared on scene shutdown, in the game **and** in each gym that draws effect visuals.
- The ring respects the existing z-order/layering conventions (drawn beneath bullets/ship as the other auras are) and does not intercept input.
- **Parent AC6 closed by this item** — **The range is visible** (Q2 = A) — a subtle **ship-centred ring** of exactly the field's current radius is drawn while the window is active and disappears when it ends, in the game and in every gym that draws power-up effect visuals, through the shared `CombatEffectVisuals` seam (one radius source, no duplicated constant, no per-frame allocation beyond what that seam already does), and it is visibly distinguishable from the Shield bubble, the Force Field bubble and the Thorn aura.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `drawChronoFieldRing` + its colour/width constants to `CombatEffectVisuals.ts`.
- Create one Graphics per scene beside the existing aura graphics; call the helper from each scene's visual update.
- Tests first: helper draw/clear/radius tests, then scene lifecycle tests.

# Pure detail model builder for centre panel

Build the pure model function that returns detail content for any focusable row key — a heading plus body lines sourced from the catalogue, economy verdicts, and deployment builder.

## Goal

Create `buildHangarDetail(screenModel, key)` that returns, for any focusable row key, a heading plus body lines:
- The catalogue description
- Kind-specific facts (hull stats, weapon matchup, modifier effect, power-up state)
- Economy price/state verdicts (price, owned, gated, unaffordable, upgradable, capped, blocked)
- For no-focus fallback: the deployment summary from buildHangarDeployment

## Acceptance Criteria

- A detail entry exists for every row kind: unlock rows, hulls, weapons, modifiers, power-ups, saved builds, deploy, map, restart, buildout
- Every unlock state is covered: owned, buyable, gated, unaffordable, upgradable, upgrade-unaffordable, capped, blocked
- Moving focus (keyboard tab/arrows, and pointer hover) onto any hangar row triggers the detail builder which updates the centre detail panel that names the option and shows its detail: the catalogue description, the option's kind-specific facts (a hull's base defence, upgrade levels, run stats and granted skill; a weapon's matchup verdict and permanent level/cap; a modifier's effect in words; a power-up's installed/off/blocked state, level and cap), and its price / owned / gated / shortfall state — every fact sourced from the shipped catalogue and the existing pure economy verdicts, with no new gameplay number invented in the screen
- The no-focus fallback returns the deployment summary (hull, weapons, modifiers, power-ups, target hex) built by the existing pure deployment builder, so the panel can never describe a launch the screen does not perform
- All content is pure — no Phaser dependencies, fully table-testable
- A new test file hangarScreen.detail.test.ts contains table tests covering every row kind and state
- Full test suite passes

## Constraints

- No new gameplay numbers authored — all facts sourced from existing catalogue, economy, and deployment builders
- The detail model is part of the HangarScreenModel (pure), not computed inside the renderer
- CVD-safe: no information conveyed by colour alone; state words/markers accompany every tint

## Key Files

- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts — new buildHangarDetail function, integrated into HangarScreenModel
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.detail.test.ts (new) — table tests for the detail builder

# Feature: Price ladder for the derived hangar weapons (and the evolution halves)

Discovered-from: AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 (producer decision Q2, intake 2026-11-25: "file separately").

## Problem
AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 derives a hangar weapon entry for every shipped `weapons.csv` row (16 CSV weapons − `cannon` exclusion = 15 entries), but ships them **grant-only**: its `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` table carries only the four already-shipped prices (`spread` starter, `wave_laser` 120/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `cluster` 160/1). Everything the tree does not already sell — the five hex-granted ids (`rapid`, `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova`) and the six sourceless ids (`options`, `mortar`, `rear_guard`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`) — is representable, grantable and visible once owned, but never purchasable.

That is the deliberate minimum fix for the referential-integrity defect. It leaves two product gaps, which this item owns:

- **No purchase path** for eleven shipped weapons a player can see in the tree but never buy.
- **Three weapon evolutions are dead.** `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` authors `ricochet` + `arc` → Chain Ricochet, `cluster` + `mortar` → Cluster Barrage and `spread` + `options` → Fan Escort, but `arc`, `mortar` and `options` cannot be owned, so the owned tier can never fire. (`arc` becomes ownable only through the `hex-r2-1` grant.)

## What this item must decide and deliver
- Which of the eleven derived weapons are actually sold, with a producer-approved `price { minerals, cores }` and `minRing` per row, calibrated against the shipped anchors (`hardened_plating` 80/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `anti_maw_plating` 110/2, `wave_laser` 120/1, `bomb` 130/1, `cluster` 160/1, `magnet` 200/2, `hull-2` 220/3, `hull-3` 320/4, `hull-4` grant-only).
- Whether promoting `arc`, `mortar` and `options` is intended to switch the three authored evolutions on, and the calibration of that new pathway (`OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL = 2` today).
- Verification that the enlarged sellable set does not distort the economy: the six-slot active cap, the auto-loadout variety rule, the ring-aggression budget (`STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0`, so weapons should not inflate `resolvePlayerStrength`) and the attract bot's `cheapestUsefulUnlock` ordering / pinned ring-timing unlock pace (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`).

## Constraints
- Prices are **authored data**, never derived from shipped tuning (see `src/utils/weapons.ts` "Baselines are frozen history"): retuning `subdivisions` must not reprice the tree.
- Only add rows to `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`; do not hand-author weapon entries — the entry, its name, description and `weaponId` stay derived (AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 AC1/AC6).
- No save-schema change; `hangar.unlockedWeapons` already carries every id.
- Any change to unlock pace must be re-baselined in the same change, or the bot's seeded traversal replays break.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The chosen price/ring table is recorded on this item with its reasoning before code is written.
- Each newly sellable weapon has a test asserting `canBuy` gating and affordability at its `minRing`.
- A test asserts no CSV tuning field feeds any catalogue `price` or `minRing` (extends AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 AC6).
- If the evolutions are switched on: a test proves the owned tier fires for each pairing, and the six-slot cap plus auto-loadout variety rule still hold.
- The ring-aggression budget is unchanged for a fleet with more weapons owned, demonstrated by the existing budget tests rather than asserted.
- Any unlock-pace change is re-baselined with the traversal replays.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact
Players can eventually buy the weapons they can already see in the hangar tree, and the three authored weapon fusions become reachable instead of being dead code.

## Out of scope
- The derivation mechanism itself and the referential-integrity guards (AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91).
- Power-up and hull derivation.
- The uncatalogued ring-2 modifier grants (AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWW69GDL002OQV6** – Randomize the hex war starter weapon (open)
- **AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91** – Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon entries from weapons.csv (open)
- **AH-0MWWI3KIO001DY5C** – Derive hangar weapon entries from the runtime weapon catalogue (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac6, acceptance, active, actually (+228 more)
- `README.md` — matched: ac1, acceptance, active, actually, add (+218 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: ac1, acceptance, active, add, aggression (+182 more)


## Intake brief (addendum — 2026-11-25)

### Problem statement (sharpened)
AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 will derive a hangar weapon entry for every `weapons.csv` row but ship them grant-only, so eleven shipped weapons are visible-but-never-buyable and the three authored fusions (`ricochet`+`arc`, `cluster`+`mortar`, `spread`+`options`) can never reach their owned tier. This item decides the sellable subset, its authored `price`/`minRing` ladder, and whether to switch those fusions on.

### Current state (verified in repo)
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` today: 4 hulls, 4 weapons (`spread` starter, `wave_laser` 120/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `cluster` 160/1), 2 modifiers, 2 power-ups. No `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` yet — it is created by AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 (currently `plan_complete`).
- Derived-but-unsellable (11): five hex-granted (`rapid`, `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova`) and six sourceless (`options`, `mortar`, `rear_guard`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). `cannon` is the exclusion.
- `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100`; `purchaseWeight(price) = minerals + cores × 100`.
- Price anchors (weight): `hardened_plating` 80/1 (180), `ricochet` 90/2 (290), `anti_maw_plating` 110/2 (310), `wave_laser` 120/1 (220), `bomb` 130/1 (230, power-up), `cluster` 160/1 (260), `magnet` 200/2 (400, power-up), `hull-2` 220/3 (520), `hull-3` 320/4 (720), `hull-4` grant-only.
- Evolution pairings (`src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts`): `ricochet`+`arc` → Chain Ricochet, `cluster`+`mortar` → Cluster Barrage, `spread`+`options` → Fan Escort. `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL = 2`.
- Eco guards: `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`; `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0` (owning more weapons adds 0 to `resolvePlayerStrength`); auto-loadout caps **one weapon per behaviour family** (families: `plain` covers `dual`/`rapid`/`rear_guard`/`shard_swarm`/`heavy_slug`/`railgun`; `spread`=`broadside`; `aoe`=`nova`/`mortar`/`arc`; `orbit`=`options`).

### Price ladder (producer-approved — Q1 = a, Q2 amended)
All eleven promoted. `options` and `broadside` were moved to ring 2 at the producer's direction and repriced into the ring-2 band; `weight` is **derived**, not authored — `purchaseWeight(price) = minerals + cores × CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT`, `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`). It is the real cost in mineral-equivalents and the value `cheapestUsefulUnlock` minimises to order the attract bot's purchases.

| weapon | behaviour family | minRing | price (minerals/cores) | weight | rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dual` | plain | 1 | 100 / 1 | 200 | twin-bullet entry tier, just above the life kit |
| `rear_guard` | plain | 1 | 130 / 1 | 230 | rear coverage utility; matches `bomb` |
| `shard_swarm` | plain | 1 | 140 / 1 | 240 | swarm filler between `cluster` and `ricochet` |
| `rapid` | plain | 1 | 110 / 2 | 310 | high cadence; sits at `anti_maw_plating` |
| `heavy_slug` | plain | 1 | 150 / 2 | 350 | slow heavy hitter |
| `options` | orbit | 2 | 200 / 2 | 400 | orbit tool + Fan Escort half; ring-2 entry, matches `magnet` |
| `broadside` | spread | 2 | 210 / 2 | 410 | wide volley fan; ring 2 (already its hex-grant ring) |
| `mortar` | aoe | 2 | 220 / 2 | 420 | Cluster Barrage half; ring-2 aoe |
| `railgun` | plain (pierce) | 2 | 230 / 2 | 430 | deep pass-through |
| `nova` | aoe | 2 | 240 / 2 | 440 | strongest ring-2 area weapon |
| `arc` | aoe | 2 | 250 / 3 | 550 | aoe + 2 chains + Chain Ricochet half |

Every ring-1 row stays above `hardened_plating` (180); every ring-2 row is at or above the `magnet` ring-2 anchor (400).

### Evolution decision (producer-approved — Q3 = a)
All three authored fusions are switched **on**: `ricochet`+`arc` → Chain Ricochet, `cluster`+`mortar` → Cluster Barrage, `spread`+`options` → Fan Escort. `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL` stays **2**. Because `ricochet`, `cluster` and `spread` are already buyable/owned and `arc`, `mortar`, `options` are now sellable, all three owned tiers become reachable — all three halves sit at ring 2, so each fusion opens in ring 2. No resolver change is expected: the fusions become live through the enlarged ownable set.

### Routine research findings (resolved in-session, no producer input needed)
- **R1 — Bot order:** `cheapestUsefulUnlock` picks minimum `purchaseWeight` among `isBotPurchaseCandidate` (all non-power-up) entries that are affordable. Today's ring-1 minimum is `hardened_plating` (180), then `wave_laser` (220). Any new ring-1 row priced below an anchor the bot currently buys **changes the seeded traversal**; either keep new rows above the anchor they must not pre-empt a purchase of, or regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` in the same change (AC already requires re-baselining on any pace change). The ladder above prices every new row ≥ 200, but a 200-weight `dual` still pre-empts `wave_laser` (220) as the *second* purchase — so **expect a re-baseline** unless the producer prefers a carve-out.
- **R2 — Aggression budget:** `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0`, so owning more weapons cannot inflate `resolvePlayerStrength` / ring aggression. Existing budget tests should still be run (AC5) but no code change is expected.
- **R3 — Cap & variety:** `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` and the one-per-family variety rule are unchanged; more candidate weapons only change *which* weapon fills a family slot, never the cap.
- **R4 — Save schema:** `hangar.unlockedWeapons` already carries every id; promoting rows is a data-only change, no migration.
- **R5 — Sourceless set confirmed:** `options`, `mortar`, `rear_guard`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug` are granted by no hex in `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`; `arc` is granted by `hex-r2-1` only.

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers
1. **Q1 — scope.** Which of the eleven derived weapons become sellable?
   - (a) All eleven; (b) the three evolution halves only; (c) the six sourceless ids only.
   - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-25 session reply): "1. A"** — all eleven become sellable. Source: interactive reply.
2. **Q2 — the price/ring ladder.** Approve the recommended table or amend it.
   - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-25 session reply): "move options and broadside into ring 2, adjust price and weight accordingly"** — applied: `options` → ring 2 at 200/2 (weight 400), `broadside` → ring 2 at 210/2 (weight 410); the remaining ring-2 rows were re-spaced (`mortar` 220/2, `railgun` 230/2, `nova` 240/2) to keep distinct, ring-2-appropriate weights around the `magnet` 400 anchor. Producer also asked **"what is weight?"** — answered: not an authored field; `purchaseWeight(price) = minerals + cores × 100`, the mineral-equivalent cost the bot's `cheapestUsefulUnlock` minimises. Source: interactive reply.
3. **Q3 — evolutions.** Switch the three authored fusions on?
   - (a) Switch all three on, keep `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL = 2`; (b) switch on but lower to 1; (c) keep off.
   - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-25 session reply): "3. A"** — switch all three on, keep `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL = 2`. Source: interactive reply.

### Consequence to plan for
With `options` and `broadside` now ring-2, the ring-1 additions are `dual` (200), `rear_guard` (230), `shard_swarm` (240), `rapid` (310), `heavy_slug` (350). `dual` at 200 still sits below `wave_laser` (220), so the attract bot's purchase order can shift and `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is expected to need regeneration in the same change (AC already requires re-baselining on any pace change).

## Goal

Withdraw the level-row deletion from the one pure consumption rule. The owned
sets are still spent and the hangar still resets to the starter kit; only the
filtering of `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` by `consumedIds` is removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A completed hex-map battle (win **or** loss) still removes the flown hull, every starting weapon and every modifier from `unlockedHulls` / `unlockedWeapons` / `ownedModifiers`, and still resets the hangar to the starter kit with an empty `activeLoadout`; **only** the level-row deletion is withdrawn — every `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` row survives `consumeDeployedShip` untouched (level and order preserved).
- The ring-end hangar-falls reset still wins over consumption: a failed ring assault returns the byte-identical fresh campaign, with no bought levels carried across the reset.
- `consumeDeployedShip` stays pure, total and idempotent — a repeated call on an already-consumed hangar returns an equal hangar, the caller's hangar is never mutated, a corrupt or unknown ship id never throws, and both banked balances are untouched.
- The `consumeDeployedShip` doc comment in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` is rewritten: a battle spends **ownership only**, and the consumed ids' bought permanent levels are retained.
- The rule stays in the one pure reducer — the game, the `GymHexWar` gym, the capture cycle and the PlayScene sortie all route through it, and no consumer re-implements or forks it (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- The targeted reducer and capture-cycle suites (`hangarEconomy.test.ts`, `consumeOnBattleEnd.test.ts`) pass with the flipped retention expectations.

## Goal

Prove the player-facing consequence end-to-end: a consumed, previously-levelled
weapon comes back at its retained level when re-bought at the normal unlock
price, and the retained row never counts as evidence of ownership anywhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Re-buying a consumed, previously-levelled weapon in the hangar costs exactly its catalogue unlock price (no upgrade re-purchase, no extra unlock step) and the next deployment grants it at the retained permanent level — a lost `wave_laser` row `{ id: 'wave_laser', level: 3 }` re-bought → `resolveActiveLoadout` + `carriedWeaponLevels` deploy `wave_laser` at level 3, and its hangar row reads `LV 3/5` with the priced next-level action.
- A retained level row never resurrects ownership: a consumed id with a surviving row is still absent from its owned set, is not installed by `buildHangarDeployment` / `resolveActiveLoadout`, is not offered by the auto-fit or the ⚡ buildout row, adds nothing to `resolvePlayerStrength`, and its hangar row stays a purchase row (`buyable` / `unaffordable` / `gated`) until it is bought again.
- Power-up behaviour is not widened by retention: `ownedLevelBearingPowerUpLevels` and the documented power-up ownership tolerance are unchanged, and a consumed power-up row behaves exactly as before.

# Test: randomised starter weapon contract (test-first)

## Summary

Write the failing (red-first) unit tests that pin the shared randomised-starter
contract — the ring-1 draw pool, the seeded draw, the per-war record, the legacy
fallback and the auto-equipped, no-cost fresh payload — before any production
code exists.

## Context

Parent AH-0MWW69GDL002OQV6. The contract this item pins (agreed names, so the
implementation items can make the tests green without renaming them):

- `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)` — the draw pool: every `kind === 'weapon'`
  entry with `minRing <= 1` and `isPurchasableEntry(entry)`.
- `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)` — the seeded draw over that pool.
- `resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar, catalogue?)` — the war's starter, falling back
  to the legacy `spread` (`STARTER_WEAPON_ID`) when the hangar predates the field.
- `HangarState.starterWeaponId?: string` — the additive per-war record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests exist and fail for the expected reason (module/field absent) for
  `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)`: it returns only ring-1 purchasable weapon
  entries, includes `spread` itself, excludes `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING` entries,
  excludes hulls/modifiers/power-ups, and picks up a weapon injected through a
  test catalogue (proving the pool iterates data, never a hard-coded list).
- Tests pin `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)` determinism: the same seed
  yields the same id on repeated calls and from independent calls, a sweep over
  at least 512 distinct seeds reaches every eligible id (reachability), a
  single-entry catalogue always returns that entry, and the draw never touches
  `Math.random` (proved by a stubbed/guarded RNG or a source assertion).
- Tests pin `resolveStarterWeaponId`: a present `starterWeaponId` is returned;
  an absent field resolves to the legacy `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` (`spread`).
- Tests pin the fresh payload from `createDefaultPayload(seed)`:
  `hangar.starterWeaponId` equals `drawStarterWeaponId(seed)`, the id is in
  `hangar.unlockedWeapons`, `hangar.activeLoadout.startingWeapons` is exactly
  `[starterId]`, `bankedMinerals`/`bankedCores` stay `0` even when the drawn
  entry's catalogue price is non-zero, and two payloads from the same seed are
  deep-equal.
- The new tests live beside the modules they pin (`hangarWarStore.test.ts`,
  `hangarEconomy.test.ts`, `hangarDeployment.test.ts`) or in a new
  `starterWeapon.test.ts`; no production behaviour is changed by this item.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/starterWeapon.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`
