# Per-war starter draw, ownership and free auto-equip

## Summary

Give every fresh Hangar War a seeded, ring-1 starter weapon that it owns for the
war and auto-equips for the first deployment, replacing the catalogue's fixed
`starter: true` weapon ownership with the per-war record.

## Acceptance Criteria

_The parent acceptance criteria this item owns, restated verbatim so the plan's AC coverage is traceable:_

- A **fresh war** (`createDefaultPayload(<seed>)` or a first load with no save) draws one starter from **every purchasable ring-1 weapon** in the hangar catalogue (`kind === 'weapon'`, `minRing <= 1`, `isPurchasableEntry`) and **auto-equips** it in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, so the very first deployment (`buildHangarDeployment`) carries it as a starting weapon. The draw is **deterministic for the payload seed** (the same seed always yields the same starter; different seeds can yield different starters, and a seeded sweep shows every eligible entry is reachable). The drawn starter costs nothing — no minerals or cores are deducted, even when its catalogue price is non-zero. (this item implements and tests it.)
- **Existing saves are unchanged**: a stored payload keeps its current owned starter, loadout and hangar state (no re-roll on load, no loadout rewrite, no back-fill). Migration stays field-presence based, no schema version bump is required, and a legacy save's implicit starter remains `spread`; a legacy save's empty loadout is still filled by the existing hangar auto-fit on open, not by this change. (this item's migration/round-trip tests cover it.)
- A new pure module exports `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)` and
  `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)`: the pool is every `kind === 'weapon'`
  entry with `minRing <= 1` and `isPurchasableEntry(entry)` (so `spread` is in
  the pool and grant-only entries are not), and the draw goes through
  `createHangarWarRng(seed).pick(...)` — no `Math.random()` anywhere in the path.
- `HangarState` gains the additive optional `starterWeaponId?: string`;
  `parseHangar` migrates it by field presence (absent stays absent, a present
  value is trimmed to a usable id) and `resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar,catalogue?)`
  returns it, falling back to `spread` when absent. No schema version bump.
- `createDefaultPayload(seed)` records the drawn id in `hangar.starterWeaponId`,
  owns it in `hangar.unlockedWeapons` and auto-equips it in
  `hangar.activeLoadout.startingWeapons`; banked minerals/cores stay `0`
  (the drawn starter is free even when its catalogue price is non-zero).
- `ownsEntry` reports the war's starter as owned even when a corrupt save
  dropped it from `unlockedWeapons`, so the fleet can never lose its free
  weapon; the catalogue's `starter: true` no longer marks any weapon (only
  `hull-1` stays a starter entry) and `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` is re-documented as
  the legacy fallback constant it now is.
- A **first load with no stored save** (`loadHangarWarPayload` against an empty
  store) yields that same fresh payload, so the very first war's starter is the
  seed's draw (no unseeded randomness on the load path).
- `buildHangarDeployment(payload)` for a fresh payload carries the drawn starter
  in the launch data's starting weapons (its permanent-level resolution is
  unchanged).
- Unit coverage: the tests from the test-first child go green, plus ownership
  and migration cases for a legacy hangar (no field) and a corrupt-starter case;
  `docs`/module docblocks touched here state the new rule (doc text itself is
  the documentation child's scope).

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/starterWeapon.ts` (new)
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`

# Starter survives battle-end consumption

## Summary

Key `consumeDeployedShip`'s starter protection to the war's drawn starter instead
of the fixed `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`, so a battle can never spend the fleet's only
free weapon on a win or a loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

_The parent acceptance criteria this item owns, restated verbatim so the plan's AC coverage is traceable:_

- The randomised starter is **owned and free for that war**, is never consumed by `consumeDeployedShip` on **win or loss**, and is protected exactly as today's `spread` starter is — so no battle outcome can leave the fleet without a free weapon (no soft-lock). Its permanent level rows follow the existing starter rules. (this item's consumption tests cover it.)
- `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue?)` resolves the protected weapon
  from the hangar (`resolveStarterWeaponId`) and excludes it from the consumed
  weapon set on **win and loss** (both go through the same rule), so a drawn
  non-`spread` starter that flew the battle stays owned afterwards.
- Every other flown starting weapon and modifier is still consumed with its
  bought permanent level rows, while the war's starter keeps its level row
  (existing starter/level-row rules unchanged for the protected id).
- The post-battle hangar reset still empties `activeLoadout` and leaves the
  hangar auto-fit to fill it on open (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D preserved for the
  post-battle reset); the empty loadout remains a legal deployment.
- Idempotence and totality hold: a repeated call on an already-consumed hangar
  returns an equal hangar, and a corrupt/absent starter field cannot throw.
- Coverage: `consumeOnBattleEnd.test.ts` and `hangarEconomy.test.ts` prove the
  win and loss paths for a drawn starter, and the game-path suite
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.hangarWarConsumption.test.ts`) or the shared win
  harness proves the same rule through `PlayScene`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`

# Restart re-draw and legacy-save preservation

## Summary

Make a war restart draw a fresh starter from its fresh seed while leaving every
existing save — including a legacy payload with no starter field — exactly as it
is.

## Acceptance Criteria

_The parent acceptance criteria this item owns, restated verbatim so the plan's AC coverage is traceable:_

# Test: price ladder data contract

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J (price ladder for the derived hangar weapons and
the evolution halves). Red-first contract spec: this child lands the **tests**
that pin the ladder before the rows are added by "Add sellable weapon ladder
rows".

## Why

The ladder is authored data, not derived tuning. `src/utils/weapons.ts` states
"Baselines are frozen history", so retuning a `subdivisions` column must never
reprice the unlock tree. Today nothing pins that: `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` (added
by AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91) is derived-entry data with no price/purity contract of
its own.

## What to build

Extend `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` (or a sibling
`hangarCatalogue.priceLadder.test.ts` if the file grows unwieldy) with a
contract block that:

- pins every one of the eleven promoted ids to its approved `minRing` and
  `price { minerals, cores }` exactly as recorded in the parent's intake brief;
- asserts the purity invariant — no CSV tuning field (e.g. `subdivisions`,
  `bulletLifetime`, `maxHitPoints`) feeds any catalogue `price` or `minRing`;
- asserts the ring-band invariants: every ring-1 promoted row's
  `purchaseWeight(price)` is at or above `hardened_plating` (180), every ring-2
  promoted row's weight is at or above the `magnet` ring-2 anchor (400);
- asserts each promoted row is still a **derived** entry (its `name`,
  `description` and `weaponId` come from the derivation, no hand-authored
  weapon entry slipped in).

The specs run **red, not crash**, while `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` and its rows are
absent — the same red-first contract pattern already used in
`src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` (`PowerUpUnlockView`), so the tests can land
ahead of the data they pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The chosen price/ring table is recorded on the parent item with its reasoning before code is written, and this spec re-asserts that table row for row.
- A test asserts no CSV tuning field feeds any catalogue price or minRing, so retuning `subdivisions` never reprices the tree.
- A test pins each of the eleven promoted weapon ids to its approved minRing and price { minerals, cores }.
- A test asserts every ring-1 promoted row's purchaseWeight is at or above hardened_plating (180) and every ring-2 promoted row's weight is at or above the magnet anchor (400).
- A test asserts each promoted row keeps its derived name, description and weaponId rather than a hand-authored weapon entry.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Test: sellable weapon purchase gating

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J. Red-first contract spec: proves each newly
sellable weapon has a real purchase path, before "Add sellable weapon ladder
rows" adds the data.

## Why

`canBuy` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) is the one gate the hangar uses
for a purchase. Promoting eleven rows is only meaningful if each is actually
buyable once its ring gate is met and the fleet can afford it — and *only* once
the gate is met.

## What to build

A `describe` block covering all eleven promoted ids (`dual`, `rapid`,
`options`, `nova`, `mortar`, `arc`, `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`,
`shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`):

- **gated**: at `minRing - 1` (and at ring 0) `canBuy` reports the entry is
  ring-gated, never `affordable`;
- **affordability**: at `minRing` with exactly the row's price banked,
  `canBuy` reports affordable; one mineral short reports unaffordable;
- **purchase records ownership**: a successful purchase lands the weapon id in
  `hangar.unlockedWeapons` and debits both currencies by exactly the price;
- **already owned**: an owned entry is never re-offered as a purchase.

Cover it as a table-driven spec keyed by the ladder, so a future row addition
inherits the gate check instead of needing a new hand-written case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each newly sellable weapon has a test asserting canBuy gating and affordability at its minRing.
- A test asserts each newly sellable weapon is gated (not affordable) one ring below its minRing.
- A test asserts buying a newly sellable weapon debits the exact price and records the weapon id in hangar.unlockedWeapons.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (`canBuy`, `buy`, `purchaseWeight`)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (`createDefaultPayload`)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (`createRingState`)

## Constraints

- Tests only; no production change in this child.
- Reuse the existing ring-state and default-payload fixtures rather than
  hand-rolling save objects.

# Add sellable weapon ladder rows

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J. The single production change of the ladder: add
the eleven producer-approved `price`/`minRing` rows to `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY`
in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`.

## Why

AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 derives a hangar weapon entry for every shipped
`weapons.csv` row (15 after the `cannon` exclusion) but ships them grant-only,
so eleven are visible-but-never-buyable. This child gives each a purchase path
while leaving the entry, its name, description and `weaponId` derived.

## The approved ladder (producer Q1 = a, Q2 amended — 2026-11-25)

| weapon | behaviour family | minRing | price (minerals/cores) | weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dual` | plain | 1 | 100 / 1 | 200 |
| `rear_guard` | plain | 1 | 130 / 1 | 230 |
| `shard_swarm` | plain | 1 | 140 / 1 | 240 |
| `rapid` | plain | 1 | 110 / 2 | 310 |
| `heavy_slug` | plain | 1 | 150 / 2 | 350 |
| `options` | orbit | 2 | 200 / 2 | 400 |
| `broadside` | spread | 2 | 210 / 2 | 410 |
| `mortar` | aoe | 2 | 220 / 2 | 420 |
| `railgun` | plain (pierce) | 2 | 230 / 2 | 430 |
| `nova` | aoe | 2 | 240 / 2 | 440 |
| `arc` | aoe | 2 | 250 / 3 | 550 |

`weight` is **derived**, never authored: `purchaseWeight(price) = minerals +
cores × CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT` (`CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100`,
`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`). The four already-shipped rows
(`spread` starter, `wave_laser` 120/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `cluster` 160/1) are
unchanged.

## What to build

- Add the eleven rows to `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` in
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`. Nothing else moves: no hand-authored weapon
  entry, no save-schema change (`hangar.unlockedWeapons` already carries every
  id), no hull/power-up derivation.
- Add a short code comment next to the table recording that the prices are
  authored (calibrated against the shipped anchors) and must never be derived
  from `weapons.csv` tuning.
- Update the surrounding doc comment to describe the enlarged sellable set and
  that the three evolution halves are now purchasable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY carries all eleven promoted ids with the approved price and minRing values from the table above.
- Each newly sellable weapon has a real purchase path: canBuy reports affordable once its minRing gate is met and the fleet can afford the price.
- The derivation remains the only source of entry fields — no hand-authored weapon catalogue entry is added.
- Prices stay authored data: retuning a weapons.csv field does not change any catalogue price or minRing.
- The price ladder data contract and purchase gating tests pass.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`

- Blocked by **AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91** — `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` and the derived

- Blocked by the two red-first test children of this item ("Test: price ladder

## Out of scope

- The derivation mechanism and its referential-integrity guards.
- Any change to `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT`, `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` or the
  auto-loadout variety rule.

# Test: owned evolution reachability

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J. Proves the three authored weapon fusions
actually fire at the **owned** tier once their halves are purchasable
(producer Q3 = a: all three switched on, `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL` stays 2).

## Why

`src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` authors `ricochet` + `arc` → Chain Ricochet,
`cluster` + `mortar` → Cluster Barrage and `spread` + `options` → Fan Escort,
but `arc`, `mortar` and `options` cannot be owned today, so the owned tier is
dead code. After the ladder lands they become ownable — this child is the proof
that the fusion is reachable **through normal play** and that the economy guards
still hold.

No resolver change is expected: the tier becomes live through the enlarged
ownable set. If the test shows a change *is* needed, record the reason on this
item before making it.

## What to build

Extend `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.test.ts` (plus the auto-loadout suite where
the cap/variety assertions belong) with:

- **reachability per pairing**: for each of the three pairings, start from a
  save that can only own weapons the catalogue actually sells, buy/level both
  halves to `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL`, keep both live in the active set, and
  assert `resolveWeaponEvolution` returns that `evolvedId` with
  `reason: 'owned'`;
- **half-purchase sanity**: assert `arc`, `mortar` and `options` are all
  purchasable (`isPurchasableEntry` / `canBuy`) — the property that un-deads
  the tiers;
- **cap**: owning all fifteen weapons never activates more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (6) weapon slots;
- **variety**: the auto-loadout still caps **one weapon per behaviour family**
  (`plain`, `spread`, `aoe`, `orbit`) once every candidate is owned, so more
  candidates change *which* weapon fills a family slot, never how many.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test proves the owned tier fires for each pairing, and the six-slot cap plus auto-loadout variety rule still hold for a fleet owning every weapon.
- A test proves the owned tier fires with reason 'owned' for each of chain_ricochet, cluster_barrage and fan_escort once both halves are owned at level 2 and live.
- A test asserts arc, mortar and options are each purchasable, which is what makes the three fused pairings reachable.
- A test asserts the auto-loadout still caps one weapon per behaviour family once every weapon is owned, so more candidates never add slots.
- Any resolver change needed is recorded with its reason on this work item; no resolver change is made speculatively.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Test: economy guards with expanded fleet

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J. Demonstrates — with tests, not assertions in
prose — that a larger sellable set cannot distort the salvage economy or the
ring-aggression budget, and pins the attract bot's new purchase order.

## Why

The ladder promotes eleven rows, five of them at ring 1 with weights 200–350.
`cheapestUsefulUnlock` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) minimises
`purchaseWeight` among affordable `isBotPurchaseCandidate` entries, so a
200-weight `dual` now pre-empts `wave_laser` (220) as the fleet's second
purchase. Two properties must be shown rather than assumed:

- **Aggression budget is unchanged.** `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0`, so
  owning more weapons adds 0 to `resolvePlayerStrength`; the ring-aggression
  budget for a max-ownership fleet must equal the shipped budget. Demonstrate
  it through the **existing** budget helpers
  (`ringAggressionBudget`, `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) — do not assert a new hand-computed
  number.
- **The bot's order is still sane and now pinned.** Record the new
  `cheapestUsefulUnlock` sequence for a seeded ring-1 fleet and pin it, so a
  future price edit is a loud test failure rather than a silent pace drift.
  This is the test counterpart to the "Re-baseline unlock pace" child.

## What to build

- A spec that builds a fleet owning **every** purchasable weapon, resolves
  player strength and the ring-aggression budget through the existing helpers,
  and asserts the budget equals the shipped baseline fleet's budget.
- A spec pinning `cheapestUsefulUnlock`'s ordered picks for a seeded ring-1

  then `dual` 200 ahead of `wave_laser` 220 — confirm against the shipped
  table and record the actual order in a comment on this item).
- A spec asserting every promoted row is a bot purchase candidate
  (`isBotPurchaseCandidate` true) — nothing in the ladder is silently excluded
  from the bot's choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ring-aggression budget is unchanged for a fleet with more weapons owned, demonstrated by the existing budget tests rather than asserted as a new hand-computed number.
- A test pins the attract bot's cheapestUsefulUnlock purchase order for a seeded ring-1 fleet with the enlarged ladder, so any future price edit fails loudly.

# Re-baseline unlock pace

Child of AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J. Regenerates the pinned ring-timing baseline for
the enlarged sellable set and updates the expectations that consume it, so the
seeded traversal replays stay green.

## Why

`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` pins the attract bot's seeded traversal
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` compares against it). The ladder adds five
ring-1 rows, and `dual` at weight 200 pre-empts `wave_laser` (220) as the second
purchase, so the seeded purchase order *will* shift. The parent's constraint is
explicit: any change to unlock pace is re-baselined **in the same change**, or
the bot's seeded traversal replays break.

## What to build

- Run `npm run ring-timing` (see `scripts/ring-timing.mjs`) to regenerate
  `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` against the enlarged ladder.
- Update any pinned expectations in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` and any
  other consumer of the baseline that hard-codes a purchase order or ring
  timing (search for the file name across `src/` and `docs/`).
- If the drift makes a documented ring-timing target unreachable (e.g. a
  ring-2 unlock arriving materially later/earlier), **stop and record it as an
  OPEN QUESTION** on this item rather than silently re-pinning a bad pace — the
  producer owns pace targets.
- Record the before/after first-purchase sequence and the ring-1/ring-2
  completion times in a comment on this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Any unlock-pace change is re-baselined with the traversal replays: docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json is regenerated in the same change as the ladder rows.
- The ring-timing and traversal-replay tests pass against the regenerated baseline.
- The before/after purchase sequence and ring completion timings are recorded on this work item.
- If the drift breaks a documented pace target, it is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION on this item instead of being silently re-pinned.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

data.description:
# Bot takes the cheap pickups it flies past without abandoning a strong enemy screen

## Problem statement

The competent bot already runs a two-layer primary/secondary model: minerals,
power-ups and asteroids are *secondaries* that may only interrupt the standing
primary when their `diversionPayoff` clears `diversionThreshold` and the primary
is not urgent. Two gaps make that model miss the producer's ask.

- **The payoff ignores distance.** `powerUpPayoff` scans every live drop for its
  content value and never looks at where the drop is
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`), and `mineralDiversionPayoff` sums the
  value of the cluster around the nearest mineral without regard to the ship's
  position. A drop 20 px away and the same drop 800 px away earn exactly the same
  divert, so "opportunistic retrieval of a *nearby* pickup" cannot be expressed.
- **The focus signal ignores enemy strength.** The `engage-enemy` primary's
  urgency is `world.wavePressure`, which is purely time-based
  (`computeWavePressure` in `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`). Enemy *strength*
  (high-threat archetypes, elites, a boss formation) never raises the bar, so the
  bot keeps sweeping while a strong screen is on it — and, conversely, nothing
  rewards sweeping once the screen thins apart from the enemy-count relaxation.

At the shipped tuning (`src/data/bot-tuning.json`: `powerUpBase=4`,
`mineralBase=4`, `enemyBase=13`, `powerUpSeekRange=850`, `mineralSeekRange=225`)
an ordinary power-up (content value `1`) produces a base payoff of `0` and only
ever diverts through `diversionOpportunity`, which with three or more live
enemies mid-wave is `0`. Ordinary weapon upgrades and most power-ups therefore
never earn a diversion, however close they are.

## Users

- **Players watching or playtesting the bot flight** (attract/demo mode and the
  bot-flight runs used for balance) — the bot must look like a sensible human:
  it grabs a weapon upgrade or a mineral cluster sitting on its path, and it
  bears down on a genuinely strong enemy screen instead of drifting off for a
  marginal pickup.
- **The producer** — owns the flight-feel trade between collection aggression
  and enemy focus; the current bot is the wrong side of that trade in both
  directions depending on the screen.
- **The designer/balance owner** — the bot's collection drives the measured
  per-deployment economy, so how willing it is to divert changes the numbers the
  unlock tree is balanced against.

Example user stories:

- *As a player watching the demo bot, I want it to sweep up a weapon upgrade
  lying in its path, so it looks like it is playing the game rather than ignoring
  free upgrades.*
- *As a player, I want the bot to turn and fight when the screen is full of
  tanks, divers and a boss, and only grab pickups when that is cheap.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **A baseline is recorded before the behaviour changes.** The shipped competent
   bot is measured over seeds 1–3 on the shipped one-level campaign
   (`node scripts/evaluate.mjs --batch --policy competent --seeds 3 --json --out eval-output/opportunistic-collection-baseline`)
   and its `aggregate` figures for `powerUps`, `enemiesDestroyed`,
   `avoidableHits`, `mineralsPerMinute` and the purposefulness/churn counters are
   recorded in the work item with the command that reproduces them.
2. **Diversion payoff is proximity-aware.** A collection opportunity's payoff
   rises as the pickup gets closer ("cheap to take") independently of its
   content value, so that an ordinary power-up/weapon drop or a lone nearby
   mineral that today never earns a diversion **can** earn one when it is close,
   while the same drop far away still cannot. The rule is symmetric for the
   mineral and power-up secondaries (one shared payoff mechanism, no per-drop
   special cases).
3. **Enemy strength raises the bar, and a strong screen wins.** A threat-pressure
   signal derived from the live enemies' registered content `threat` weights
   (plus boss/elite presence where the world model exposes it) raises the
   `engage-enemy` primary's urgency, so while a threat-heavy screen is present
   even a nearby pickup does not divert the bot; as the screen thins the existing
   `diversionOpportunity` relaxation takes over and the bot sweeps.
4. **Hard constraints are untouched.** Survival, `secure-life` and
   `engage-boss` remain hard primaries: no diversion is possible while any of
   them is valid, and no acceptance of this item may weaken them.
5. **Measured outcome on the same seeds.** Mean `powerUps` collected per
   deployment is **strictly greater** than the recorded baseline while mean
   `enemiesDestroyed` does not fall by more than 5 % and mean `avoidableHits`
   does not increase. If no tuning reaches that without a churn regression, the
   highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to them and the
   residual gap is filed as a linked balance item — the measured result stands
   rather than the target being silently restated.
6. **Movement churn does not regress.** On the same seeded runs the
   purposefulness metrics (committed-goal switch rate, mean hold) and the
   turn-churn counters (turn duty cycle, turn flips/reversals, forward toggles,
   reverse presses) stay at or below the shipped bot — the producer's earlier
   "bot oscillates too much" objection (AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2) must not return.
7. **Everything is tunable-driven.** Every new or changed threshold is a named
   competent tunable with a default, a tooltip entry in `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`
   and a value in the shipped `src/data/bot-tuning.json` baseline; no magic
   numbers in the goal or commitment code, and the knobs are reachable from the
   bot-tuning gym (`GymBotTuning`).
8. **Deterministic tests pin both sides of the rule.** Unit tests cover the
   payoff and threat-pressure functions (near vs far, ordinary vs strong drop,
   thin vs strong screen, torus wraparound), and two-layer selection tests pin
   that a nearby ordinary drop diverts on a thin screen and does **not** divert
   on a strong screen or while a hard primary is valid. Same seed still yields
   the same decision sequence.
9. **Documentation is updated** — `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 (priority bands
   and the two-layer model) and any quoted figures, plus code comments on the new
   tunables; the GDD is touched only if it quotes a changed behaviour or figure.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Players watching or playing alongside the bot see it grab the weapon upgrades
and minerals that lie on its path while still turning to fight when the screen is
genuinely dangerous, instead of ignoring cheap pickups and drifting off mid-fight.

## Constraints

- **Scope boundary with the in-flight mineral work.** Physical *collection
  routing* (how the bot flies to a pickup: route-through/intercept, no precision
  braking) is owned by the route-through collection re-tune
  (AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J / AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P) and the harness-fidelity items
  (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ, AH-0MWT5C*). This item changes **which** target the bot
  commits to and **how willing** it is to detour — not how it flies the
  collection. Mineral income targets stay with that epic; this item only shares
  the payoff mechanism.
- **No micro-positioning.** The producer rejected precise positioning and
  retro-braking onto pickups (AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 audit rejection): the new
  payoff must make the bot *choose* cheap pickups, never chase a pickup's exact
  centre. `collectReverseBrake` stays off and `collectOvershootMargin` stays as
  shipped unless the item explicitly argues otherwise.
- **Gym↔game parity** is automatic here: the change lives in the shared competent
  brain, so `PlayScene` and every bot-driving gym consume the same code; no
  divergent copies.
- **Determinism** (same seed → same decisions) is a hard invariant of the
  framework (`docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §6).
- **Measurement cost.** The campaign measurement is minutes-scale; run it at the
  documented points only (baseline, post-change), not per iteration.

## Existing state

- Goals, bands and the two-layer model: `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`
  (`createCompetentGoals`, `diversionOpportunity`, `mineralDiversionPayoff`,
  `powerUpPayoff`), applied by
  `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts::selectTwoLayerGoal`.
- Enemy-focus urgency is `world.wavePressure` (`computeWavePressure` in
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`) — time only.
- Content profiles that carry the per-drop `value` and per-enemy `threat`:
  `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`.
- Tunables: `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`; live-edit surface
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`; shipped values `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; the
  bot-tuning gym `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`.
- Measurement: `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/` (`metrics.ts` reports
  `powerUps`, `enemiesDestroyed`, `avoidableHits`; `purposefulness.ts` and
  `turnChurn.ts` are the churn guards).
- Known presets that already lean this way: `cautious-collector` in
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (`mineralBase=8`, `powerUpBase=8`,
  `mineralSeekRange=600`, `powerUpSeekRange=1300`) — evidence that a
  tuning-only change is not enough, because the payoff gate, not the band, is
  what blocks ordinary drops.

## Desired change

1. Make a collection opportunity's diversion payoff reflect **how cheap it is to
   take** (distance from the ship, and the detour off the current course), not
   only what it is worth. The intent is: a nearby ordinary pickup becomes worth
   a diversion; the same pickup across the arena stays not worth one; a red
   mineral deposit or a strong/rare drop is still worth a longer detour than a
   lone gold dot.
2. Feed **enemy strength** into the enemy primary's urgency: a threat-pressure
   signal from the live enemies' content weights (and boss/elite presence where
   available), so "focus on the enemy while they are particularly strong" is a
   first-class input and the diversion bar rises with it.
3. Keep the shape of the model: no new goal ids, no new bands, no change to hard
   primaries; the change is the two payoffs/urgency inputs plus their tunables.
4. Pin the behaviour with deterministic tests and the measured before/after
   figures described in the acceptance criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — proximity/detour-aware diversion payoff
  for the mineral and power-up secondaries; threat-pressure input to the
  `engage-enemy` urgency.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — new named tunables and defaults
  (e.g. an opportunistic radius, a detour-cost weight, a threat-pressure
  weight/cap).
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — expose a threat-pressure signal if it
  belongs on the world view rather than in the goal.
- `src/ai/framework/commitment.ts` — consumed as-is unless the urgency cap needs
  a companion knob.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — live-edit entries and
  shipped baseline values.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`, `commitment.test.ts`,
  `competentBot.integration.test.ts` — deterministic unit/integration coverage.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — §9.1 priority/two-layer section, and any figures.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J** — *Review the per-deployment mineral income after
  pass-through collection* (epic, in flight). Owns collection **routing** and the
  mineral income target; this item owns the diversion **priority** rule. The
  mineral payoff change here must be coordinated with its implementation slice so
  the two do not measure each other's changes as noise.
- **AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P** — *Implement route-through collection re-tune*
  (implementation slice of the above, open).
- **AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ**, **AH-0MWT5CPPL009QZWE / AH-0MWT5CQMH004ZXQK /
  AH-0MWT5CRJ600382MS / AH-0MWT5CTCO009MJ24** — arena mineral-fidelity work; the
  power-up measurement is faithful today (campaign mode uses the real per-kill
  drop rule), the mineral figure is advisory while these land.
- **AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2** — *Bot oscillates too much*: the two-layer model, the
  overshoot tolerance and the churn guards this item must not regress.
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** — *Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >
  enemies > asteroids*: the original banding and the earned-diversion rule.
- **AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68** — *AI should focus fire on the boss*: the hard-primary
  boss band that already blocks diversions.
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** — *Bot prioritises extra lives…*: the `secure-life`
  hard primary.
- **AH-0MWW2PFU8001J0PM** — *Hold station and shoot when a hit is likely*:
  posture interaction to keep in mind when the enemy primary holds.
- **AH-0MVSDM5T1007KBB8** — *Curated bot-tuning presets*: where a
  collection-aggressive preset would live if this lands as a knob change only.
- **docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md** §9.1 (priority bands, two-layer model), §9.12
  (smooth turning and overshoot tolerance), §12 (bot-tuning gym);
  **docs/BALANCING.md** and **docs/EVALUATION.md** (measurement harness).

## Risks

- **Oscillation regression (highest).** Every lever that makes the bot turn for a
  pickup is also a lever that reintroduces the churn the producer rejected. The
  churn/purposefulness guards (AC6) are the mitigation, and the proximity payoff
  must be bounded so it never rewards a U-turn for a passed pickup.
- **Wrong focus interpretation.** If "particularly strong" meant the bot's own
  weapon power, the enemy-pressure signal alone would not satisfy the intent.
  Mitigation: keep the new pressure input behind one tunable-weighted seam so a
  second (own-strength) input can be added without restructuring.
- **Measurement noise.** Power-up drops are chance-driven, so a single seed can
  move a lot; the criterion is a mean over seeds 1–3 on identical seeds for
  baseline and candidate, not a per-seed assertion.
- **Scope creep.** "Also make it collect minerals better" overlaps the in-flight
  mineral epic; this item must resist absorbing its income target or routing
  work. Extra opportunities found during implementation are recorded as linked
  work items, not added to scope.
- **Gym-only tuning drift.** Tuning in the gym must be saved to the shipped
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` baseline, or the measurement measures a different
  bot than the game flies.

## Assumptions and open questions

Recorded in the Appendix below. No producer hold is raised: the one genuine
ambiguity (what "the enemies are particularly strong" refers to) is resolved by a
documented, cheaply reversible assumption backed by the code shape.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q: What does "focus on the enemy while they are particularly strong" refer
  to — the enemy screen's strength, or the bot's own weapon power?**
  Answer (agent, research + documented assumption): **the enemy screen's
  strength** — a threat-weighted pressure signal over the live enemies
  (content `threat` weights, boss/elite presence). Evidence: the bot snapshot
  exposes no loadout/weapon-power data at all (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` has only
  `shotSpeed` and `weaponRange`), so "the bot's weapons are strong" would need new
  snapshot wiring from `PlayScene`, whereas the enemy-side signal is already
  available through the registry the goals use. The assumption is cheaply
  reversible: it is one tunable-weighted input to the enemy primary's urgency.
  **Recommended (had the producer been asked):** the enemy-side reading. If the
  producer intended the bot's own strength, the follow-up is a snapshot-field item
  (bot weapon/loadout power in the world model) and this item's second AC becomes
  a two-sided signal.
- **Q: Is a tuning-only change (e.g. copying the `cautious-collector` preset)
  sufficient?** Answer (agent, research): no. Bands and ranges already have a
  collection-aggressive preset, but the diversion gate is the blocker: an
  ordinary drop's payoff base is `0` and the relaxation is `0` with ≥3 live
  enemies mid-wave, so raising the band or the seek range does not let a nearby
  ordinary pickup earn a diversion (`goals.ts::powerUpPayoff`,
  `diversionOpportunity`). A payoff change is required.
- **Q: Does this item duplicate the in-flight mineral income epic?** Answer
  (agent, duplicate check): no — partial overlap only. AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J owns
  route-through collection and the per-deployment income target; this item owns
  the diversion priority/payoff rule (which affects minerals *and* power-ups) and
  measures power-up pickups and enemy engagement rather than mineral income. The
  description was written to address only that difference and the linked epic is
  referenced explicitly. Search terms used: `bot`, `collect`, `mineral`,
  `powerup`, `pickup`, `divert`, `tuning`, `aggressive`.
- **Q: Which bot does this apply to — demo/attract flight, gyms, or the headless
  measurement bot?** Answer (agent, research): one shared brain.
  `PlayScene` builds `createCompetentBotBrain()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) and
  `GymBotTuning` builds the same, so a change in the competent framework applies
  to the game, every bot-driving gym and the headless measurement with no
  divergent copies (gym↔game parity convention).
- **Q: What aggressiveness target should the item be balanced to?** Answer: not
  fixed at intake. The acceptance criteria require a recorded baseline and a
  strict improvement with an explicit non-regression tolerance on enemy kills and
  avoidable hits, in the established repo style (measure, pin, record). No
  producer-chosen number is needed to start.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)
- **AH-0MV66CNAF003YROX** – Update docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md to note per-parameter tooltips (completed)
- **AH-0MWJ7EELF000ALYX** – Two-layer primary/secondary objective model (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mwj1680z001qyv2, abandoning, absorbing, ac6 (+579 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mwj1680z001qyv2, 0mww2pfu8001j0pm, abandoning, acceptance, added (+540 more)
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — matched: 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mvbmesie003yq68, 0mvsdm5t1007kbb8, 0mwj1680z001qyv2, 0mww2pfu8001j0pm (+483 more)

## Plan: decomposition

Six child items, sequenced so the baseline is captured before any behaviour
change, each behaviour change is specified by red-first tests, and the
measurement closes the loop.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Baseline: measure the shipped bot on seeds 1-3 (AH-0MWY3WAOM0039CS9) | task | — |
| 2 | Tests: proximity-aware diversion payoff (AH-0MWY3WBT000122Q9) | task | — |
| 3 | Implement proximity-aware diversion payoff (AH-0MWY3WCV3003QZ3U) | feature | #2 |
| 4 | Tests: threat pressure and two-layer gating (AH-0MWY3WDWA002UN1M) | task | #3 |
| 5 | Implement threat-pressure enemy urgency (AH-0MWY3WEZK009K7UD) | feature | #4 |
| 6 | Post-change measurement and churn guards (AH-0MWY3WG0Y000I5CY) | task | #1, #5 |

Phases are vertical slices:

1. **Measurement slice (child 1)** — harness only, no source change; pins the
   reference figures AC1 requires.
2. **Payoff slice (children 2–3)** — tests, shared payoff helper, tunables,
   tooltips, shipped values, gym reachability and the §9.1 payoff prose land
   together.
3. **Threat slice (children 4–5)** — tests, `BotWorld.threatPressure`, the
   urgency composition, tunables, tooltips, shipped values and the §9.1
   urgency prose land together.
4. **Verification slice (child 6)** — same-seed before/after comparison, churn
   guards, pinned figures and the balance fallback.

Between phases: review the next child's description against what the previous
phase actually did, and update it before starting (tracer-bullet discipline).

### AC coverage

| Parent AC | Delivered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 baseline recorded | child 1 |
| AC2 proximity-aware payoff | children 2–3 |
| AC3 enemy strength raises the bar | children 4–5 |
| AC4 hard constraints untouched | children 4–5 |
| AC5 measured outcome | child 6 |
| AC6 churn does not regress | children 1, 6 |
| AC7 tunable-driven | children 3, 5 |
| AC8 deterministic tests | children 2, 4 |
| AC9 documentation | children 3, 5, 6 |
| AC10 full suite passes | children 3, 5, 6 |

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-26 — planned by `plan` (downtime dispatch): six children created in
  test-first dependency order; baseline item first, measurement item last.
  No new producer decisions raised: the one genuine ambiguity ("particularly
  strong" enemies) stays resolved by the documented assumption already in the
  Appendix, and the elite-status question is recorded below as an OPEN
  QUESTION answered by a documented scope decision rather than a producer hold.
- 2026-11-26 — AC coverage review escalated before it passed: the first pass
  matched the parent criteria only loosely, so the helper auto-created seven
  `Close coverage gap` children (AH-0MWY3Z4ZV003C0X4, AH-0MWY3Z5XL0067BTQ,
  AH-0MWY3Z6SD002IL2Q, AH-0MWY3Z7LZ0024QWX, AH-0MWY3Z8JD005MZ51,
  AH-0MWY3Z9EK0078SLZ, AH-0MWY3ZAB30025QYI). The six plan children were then
  rewritten so each restates the parent criterion it delivers, coverage was
  re-verified at 100 % from those six alone, and the seven generated items were
  closed as duplicates of the covering plan child (their close comments name the
  replacement). The review then returned `proceed` with no new children.

## Appendix: planning session

- **Q: Should the threat-pressure signal use elite status as well as the
  boss?** Answer (agent, research): the boss yes, elites no for now.
  `BotSnapshot`/`BotEnemy` expose no elite flag
  (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`), and the world model can only partition what the
  snapshot carries; elite decoration lives on `BaseEnemy`
  (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.elite.test.ts`) but is not projected to the bot. The
  signal therefore uses content `threat` weights plus `world.boss`, which is
  the parent AC3's "where the world model exposes it" wording. Adding an elite
  flag would be a new snapshot field (a `PlayScene` change) and is deliberately
  out of scope; if the measurement (child 6) shows threat pressure is too weak to
  suppress diversions, the follow-up is a linked snapshot-field item, not a
  widening of this epic.
- **Q: Is a separate test item per behaviour change worth the overhead, or
  should tests ride with the implementation?** Answer (agent, research): separate
  test items, per the plan skill's test-first ordering. The repo already pins
  these behaviours in dedicated files (`goals.test.ts`,
  `competentBot.integration.test.ts`), so a red-first item per rule keeps the
  specification reviewable before any payoff constant is chosen.
- **Q: Does the change need to touch the legacy decision layer
  (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`), which has its own wave-pressure divert heuristic?**
  Answer (agent, research): no. The shipped game builds
  `createCompetentBotBrain()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:745`); `botDecision.ts`
  backs the legacy policy only (`src/ai/framework/legacyPolicy.ts`, evaluated as
  `--baseline legacy`). The parent's scope is the competent brain, so the legacy
  ladder is left unchanged.
- **Q: Coordination with the in-flight mineral work?** Answer (agent, research):
  recorded as a constraint, not a dependency. AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J /
  AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P own collection *routing* and the mineral income target;
  this plan changes the diversion *gate* only. Child 1 must run before either
  implementation lands where possible, and child 6 treats the mineral figure as
  advisory if the re-tune lands in the same window.
data.title: Bot needs to be more aggressive in collecting minerals and power-ups/weapon upgrades. However, we must be careful not to ignore the enemies. A reasonable strategy might be to focus on the enemy while they are particularly strong, though an opportunistic retrieval of a nearby power-up/weapon upgrade should always be considered valuable.

# Baseline: measure the shipped bot on seeds 1–3

## Target outcome

The pre-change flight of the shipped competent bot is pinned both as a
retained artifact and as recorded numbers, so every later comparison in the
parent item has a fixed reference.

## Why this comes first

Every acceptance criterion of the parent measures a *change* (AC1, AC5, AC6).
Without this snapshot an apparent "improvement" cannot be told apart from
run-to-run noise, and the parent's AC1 explicitly requires the baseline to be
recorded **before** the behaviour changes.

## Definition of done

- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --batch --policy competent --seeds 3 --json --out eval-output/opportunistic-collection-baseline`
  completes on a clean tree with the shipped `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
- The `aggregate` block (`powerUps`, `enemiesDestroyed`, `avoidableHits`,
  `mineralsPerMinute`) is recorded on this item **and** on the parent with the
  exact reproducing command.
- Purposefulness (committed-goal switch rate, mean hold) and turn-churn
  counters (turn duty cycle, turn flips/reversals, forward toggles, reverse
  presses) from the same runs are recorded alongside the aggregates.
- A repeat run on seeds 1–3 reproduces the aggregates, or the observed

# Implement proximity-aware diversion payoff

## Target outcome

A collection opportunity's diversion payoff reflects **how cheap it is to
take** — wrapped distance from the ship, and whether collecting needs a
U-turn — as well as what it is worth, through one shared mechanism used by
both the mineral and the power-up secondaries.

## Why

Today an ordinary power-up (content value 1) produces a base payoff of `0`
and a lone gold mineral `0.1`, with no distance term at all, so a drop 20 px
away and the same drop 800 px away earn an identical divert. At the shipped
tuning (`powerUpBase=4`, `mineralBase=4`, `powerUpSeekRange=850`,
`mineralSeekRange=225`) that means ordinary weapon upgrades almost never earn
a diversion, however close they are — the producer's "more aggressive
collection" ask cannot be expressed.

## Definition of done

- One shared payoff helper serves both `collect-mineral` and
  `collect-powerup` (no per-drop or per-goal special cases).
- Payoff rises monotonically as wrapped distance to the best opportunity falls
  from `opportunisticRange` to 0, independently of content value, so a nearby
  ordinary drop can clear `diversionThreshold` while a far one cannot.
- A forward/no-U-turn guard bounds the term so a passed pickup never earns a
  diversion that would reverse the ship for it.
- New named tunables (`opportunisticRange`, a proximity-weight knob and the
  U-turn guard knob) with documented defaults in `tunables.ts`.
- The proximity weight is a kill switch: `0` reproduces the pre-change payoff
  exactly, giving the A/B lever the measurement item needs.
- Each new tunable has a `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` tooltip entry, a value in
  the shipped `src/data/bot-tuning.json` baseline, and is reachable from
  `GymBotTuning`.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 describes the proximity term and lists the new
  tunables.
- The payoff tests from the sibling test item pass unchanged.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the tunables and defaults (`tunables.ts`), tooltips (`tuningFields.ts`)
   and shipped values (`bot-tuning.json`).
2. Extract the shared payoff helper in `goals.ts`: content worth (`[0,1]`) ×
   a proximity cheapness term, combined with the existing
   `diversionOpportunity` relaxation, clamped to `[0,1]`.
3. Gate the proximity term on forward-ness so only targets the ship can reach
   without a reversal contribute.
4. Point `mineralDiversionPayoff` and `powerUpPayoff` at the helper, dropping
   the cluster-only / above-neutral-only rules in favour of the shared rule
   while keeping a red deposit ahead of a lone gold dot.
5. Confirm the knobs appear in the bot-tuning gym; no gym code change should
   be needed if the existing tunable wiring is generic (verify, do not assume).

## Constraints

- **No micro-positioning.** The payoff changes *which* target is chosen, never
  how the ship flies to it. `collectReverseBrake` stays off and
  `collectOvershootMargin` stays as shipped.
- Collection **routing** (route-through/intercept) is out of scope: owned by
  AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J / AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P.
- No new goal ids, no new bands, and no change to the hard primaries.
- Gym↔game parity is automatic (shared competent brain) — no divergent copy
  in `PlayScene` or a gym.
- Determinism: the payoff is a pure function of the snapshot and tunables.

## Risky assumptions

- A distance term alone (without a heading guard) would reward a U-turn for a
  passed pickup and reintroduce the churn the producer rejected
  (AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2). Mitigation: the guard is part of this slice, not a
  follow-up.
- The shipped tuning may need `powerUpBase` / `mineralSeekRange` re-tuned as
  well. Deliberately left to the measurement item: this slice changes the
  gate, not the bands.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Diversion payoff is proximity-aware: a collection opportunity's payoff rises as the pickup gets closer ("cheap to take") independently of its content value, so that an ordinary power-up/weapon drop or a lone nearby mineral that today never earns a diversion can earn one when it is close, while the same drop far away still cannot. The rule is symmetric for the mineral and power-up secondaries (one shared payoff mechanism, no per-drop special cases).
- A single shared payoff mechanism computes the diversion payoff for both the mineral and the power-up secondaries, with no per-drop or per-goal special case.
- A forward/no-U-turn guard prevents a target behind the ship from earning a proximity-derived diversion.
- Everything is tunable-driven: every new or changed threshold is a named competent tunable with a default, a tooltip entry in `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` and a value in the shipped `src/data/bot-tuning.json` baseline; no magic numbers in the goal or commitment code, and the knobs are reachable from the bot-tuning gym (`GymBotTuning`). Setting the proximity weight to `0` reproduces the pre-change payoff.
- The sibling test item's cases pass unchanged and the changed-scope suite is green via the test skill.
- Documentation is updated — `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 (priority bands and the two-layer model) and any quoted figures, plus code comments on the new tunables; the GDD is touched only if it quotes a changed behaviour or figure.

# Tests: threat pressure and two-layer gating (red first)

## Target outcome

Deterministic tests that specify the threat-pressure signal and the two-layer
gating outcome it drives — a nearby ordinary pickup diverts on a thin screen
but not on a threat-heavy one, and never while a hard primary is valid.

## Definition of done

- New unit cases cover the threat-pressure function across: empty screen,
  neutral-threat scouts, tanks/divers, boss present, and clamping/monotonicity.
- New unit cases pin that the signal is independent of the wave clock (a strong
  screen raises urgency even with plenty of time left).
- New two-layer selection cases pin: nearby ordinary power-up diverts on a thin
  screen; the same drop does not divert on a threat-heavy screen; no diversion
  while `survive`, `secure-life` or `engage-boss` is valid.
- A determinism case pins that the same seed yields the same decision sequence.
- The cases are red before the implementation item and pass unchanged after it.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend the existing world-model unit tests with threat-pressure table cases.
2. Extend `goals.test.ts` (two-layer selection) with thin-versus-strong-screen
   cases reusing the near-opportunity fixtures from the sibling payoff test
   item.
3. Extend `competentBot.integration.test.ts` with one seeded determinism case.
4. Record the red run output in a comment.

## Constraints

- Tests must read the threat weights from `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT`, not from
  literals, so a content change cannot silently pass.
- No implementation in this item; the tunable names are fixed here so the
  implementation supplies values only.
- No timing or randomness: the screen is built from fixed snapshots.

## Risky assumptions

- The scenario "strong screen" must be built from archetypes that genuinely
  exist in the content registry (tank/diver plus a boss), not from invented
  ids — a guard in `content.test.ts` would reject an unregistered id.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Threat-pressure unit tests pin: empty screen → 0; neutral scouts → low; the same count of tanks/divers → higher; boss present → higher still; result clamped to `[0, 1]` and monotone in threat weight.
- Tests pin that threat pressure is independent of the wave clock (a strong screen raises urgency even with plenty of time left).
- Two-layer selection tests pin that a nearby ordinary power-up diverts on a thin screen and does **not** divert on a threat-heavy (strong) screen, so a strong screen wins even when a pickup is nearby; no diversion is possible while a hard primary is valid.
- An integration test pins that the same seed yields the same decision sequence.
- Tests read the threat weights from `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT` rather than literals, so a content change cannot silently pass.
- The cases are red on the pre-change code and pass unchanged once the implementation item lands.

# Implement threat-pressure enemy urgency

## Target outcome

A threat-pressure signal derived from the live enemies' registered content
`threat` weights (plus boss presence) raises the `engage-enemy` primary's
urgency, so a genuinely strong screen suppresses diversion and a thinning
screen hands back to the existing opportunistic relaxation.

## Why

The `engage-enemy` urgency is `world.wavePressure`, which is purely
time-based (`computeWavePressure`). Enemy *strength* — tanks, divers, a boss
formation — never raises the diversion bar, so the bot keeps sweeping while a
strong screen is on it. "Focus on the enemy while they are particularly
strong" is currently unrepresentable.

## Definition of done

- A threat-pressure signal in `[0, 1]` computed from live enemy content
  `threat` weights, normalised by a tunable enemy count, plus a boss term when
  `world.boss` is live.
- `engage-enemy` urgency becomes a tunable-weighted combination of
  `wavePressure` and threat pressure; the existing wave-pressure behaviour is
  preserved when the new weight is `0`.
- Hard primaries untouched: `survive`, `secure-life` and `engage-boss` still
  pre-empt every diversion.
- New tunables (threat-pressure weight, the count normaliser, and the boss
  contribution) with defaults, `tuningFields.ts` tooltips, shipped
  `bot-tuning.json` values and `GymBotTuning` reachability.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 documents the urgency composition and the new
  tunables.
- The sibling test item's cases pass unchanged.

## Minimal implementation

1. Expose the signal where it belongs: `computeThreatPressure` beside
   `computeWavePressure` in `worldModel.ts`, added to `BotWorld` as
   `threatPressure` — the same shape as the existing `wavePressure` field.
2. Weight live enemies by `content.resolveEnemy(archetype).threat`, add the
   boss term, normalise and clamp.
3. Compose the `engage-enemy` urgency in `goals.ts` from the two pressures via
   the new tunables.
4. Add the tunables, tooltips, shipped values and docs.

## Constraints

- **No new snapshot field.** Elite status is not exposed in `BotSnapshot`;
  adding it is out of scope for this epic (recorded decision, see the parent
  Appendix). The signal is content `threat` weights + boss presence.
- No new goal ids, no new bands, no change to the hard primaries.
- The change lives in the shared competent brain, so the game and every
  bot-driving gym consume it — no divergent copies.
- Deterministic and pure: no clock, no randomness, no per-tick state.

## Risky assumptions

- A threat-weighted count (rather than a raw count) is the right "strength"
  proxy. Mitigation: the normaliser and the boss term are separate tunables, so
  the signal can be re-weighted without restructuring.
- If "particularly strong" meant the bot's *own* weapon power, this signal is
  insufficient. The parent Appendix records that the enemy-side reading was
  adopted because the snapshot exposes no loadout power; the seam is one
  tunable-weighted input, so a second input can be added later without
  restructuring.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts`
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A threat-pressure signal derived from the live enemies' registered content `threat` weights (plus boss presence where the world model exposes it) raises the `engage-enemy` primary's urgency, so while a threat-heavy screen is present even a nearby pickup does not divert the bot; as the screen thins the existing `diversionOpportunity` relaxation takes over and the bot sweeps.
- `BotWorld` exposes the signal as `threatPressure` in `[0, 1]`, computed by a unit-tested pure function (no clock, no randomness, no per-tick state).
- Hard constraints are untouched: survival, `secure-life` and `engage-boss` remain hard primaries — no diversion is possible while any of them is valid, and nothing in this change weakens them.
- `engage-enemy` urgency is a tunable-weighted combination of `wavePressure` and `threatPressure`; setting the new weight to `0` reproduces the pre-change urgency exactly.
- Every new threshold is a named competent tunable with a default, a `tuningFields.ts` tooltip, a shipped `bot-tuning.json` value and `GymBotTuning` reachability; `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 documents the urgency composition and each new knob has a code comment.
- No new snapshot field is added: elite status is not exposed by `BotSnapshot` and stays out of scope (see the parent Appendix).

# Post-change measurement, churn guards and balance fallback

## Target outcome

The behaviour change is proved on the same seeds as the recorded baseline — more
power-ups collected, enemy kills and avoidable hits held, no oscillation
regression — and the guard is pinned to the measured result even if the target
is missed.

## Why

Parent AC5 and AC6 are the whole point of the change: "more aggressive
collection" that costs enemy engagement or reintroduces the churn the producer
rejected (AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2) is a regression, not an improvement.

## Definition of done

- The identical command and seeds used for the baseline are re-run against the
  new bot; the before/after figures are recorded per seed and as a mean.
- Mean `powerUps` strictly greater than baseline; mean `enemiesDestroyed` down
  by no more than 5 %; mean `avoidableHits` not increased.
- Purposefulness (committed-goal switch rate, mean hold) and turn-churn
  counters (turn duty cycle, flips/reversals, forward toggles, reverse presses)
  at or below the baseline.
- If the target is missed: the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard
  is pinned to them, and a linked balance item is filed with `wl create` — the
  measured result stands rather than the target being restated.
- Quoted figures in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 are updated to the measured
  result (the GDD only if it quotes a changed behaviour or figure).
- The full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Minimal implementation

1. Re-run the baseline command with `--out eval-output/opportunistic-collection-post`
   on the merged payoff + threat-pressure change.
2. Compare per metric with `jq` against the recorded baseline; a bounded
   calibration pass (at most three candidate tunable settings, same seeds) is
   allowed before recording.
3. Record the comparison table, the chosen tunable values and the guard values
   on this item and on the parent.
4. Update the §9.1 figures; file the balance item if the target is missed.

## Constraints

- Minutes-scale runs: the baseline plus at most three calibration runs plus the
  final run. No per-iteration campaigns.
- Never edit `.worklog` data directly and never re-record the baseline: the
  baseline is fixed by the sibling item.
- Tuning done in the bot-tuning gym must be saved back to the shipped
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json`, or the measurement measures a different bot than
  the game flies.

## Risky assumptions

- Power-up drops are chance-driven, so a single seed can move a lot; the
  criterion is a mean over seeds 1–3, not a per-seed assertion.
- If the collection re-tune (AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J / AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P) lands
  in the same window, the mineral figure is advisory; the power-up and
  enemy-engagement figures remain the decision criteria.

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs`
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/purposefulness.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts`
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json`
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measured outcome on the same seeds: mean `powerUps` collected per deployment is strictly greater than the recorded baseline while mean `enemiesDestroyed` does not fall by more than 5 % and mean `avoidableHits` does not increase. If no tuning reaches that without a churn regression, the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to them and the residual gap is filed as a linked balance item.
- The post-change batch run uses the identical command and seeds as the recorded baseline, and the before/after figures are recorded per seed and as a mean on this item and on the parent.
- Movement churn does not regress: on the same seeded runs the purposefulness metrics (committed-goal switch rate, mean hold) and the turn-churn counters (turn duty cycle, turn flips/reversals, forward toggles, reverse presses) stay at or below the shipped bot, so the producer's earlier "bot oscillates too much" objection (AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2) does not return.
- Tuning done in the bot-tuning gym is saved back to the shipped `src/data/bot-tuning.json` baseline, and the `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.1 figures match the measured result.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
